items.title: Service passport racketeering started under NPP – Vice Chair of Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee
items.description: The Vice Chairperson of Parliament’s Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration Committee, Cletus Seidu Dapalah, has accused the previous New Patriotic Party (NPP) administration of failing to address alleged service passport racketeering that he says began in 2023. He claims the alleged scheme was facilitated by Alhassan Sumani, whom he described as an intermediary who operated around the corridors of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Passport Application Centre. Speaking on JoyFM’s Top Story on Monday, November 9, Mr Dapalah also questioned the basis of the Minority’s claims over letters bearing the signature of the Ministry’s Chief Director, which allegedly approved passports for individuals holding public positions they did not occupy. The Minority has presented the letters as evidence of irregularities, but the Ministry’s spokesperson, Fred Doho, has reportedly said the signatures were forged and the documents did not originate from the Ministry. Mr Dapalah argued that the Minority had not sufficiently verified the information before making it public. “Let me state clearly that oversight is a job that comes with in-depth analysis of information gathered. When you gather information, you see the information, you interrogate the information, you double-check your facts before you put it out there. “That is what my friends on the other side feel. They haven’t been in-depth with their data. They have not double-checked. “They have no facts as far as this issue is concerned. They just got some information and they ran with it to the media to throw dust in the eyes of Ghanaians,” he said. He maintained that the alleged racketeering did not begin under the current administration, insisting that it started during the NPP’s tenure. “The issue of service passports racketeering started back in 2023. Who was in office then? It was their government (NPP) that was in power,” he said. Mr Dapalah alleged that Mr Sumani had connections within the Ministry and used them to facilitate a visa-racketeering syndicate. He further claimed that Mr Sumani had collected money from a pastor and his wife in exchange for service passports but failed to deliver all the documents. According to him, the couple had since been pursuing him for their money. The MP also questioned the presence of former Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs, Aprah Twum, at a Minority press conference on the matter, arguing that the alleged activities began when he was responsible for passport applications. He alleged that Mr Sumani was recruited into the Ministry on November 29, 2024, after the general election, at a time when the NPP was preparing to leave office. Mr Dapalah claimed that the recruitment gave Mr Sumani access to the Ministry’s letterhead, which he allegedly used to forge the Chief Director’s signature on passport-related documents. “So the same guy, once he found himself into the ministry, he had access to the ministry’s letterhead and he then used the ministry letterhead to forge the signature of the chief director,” he added

items.title: Négociations Ukraine-Russie à Abou Dhabi : que révèle la composition de la délégation russe ?
items.description: Des représentants russes et ukrainiens se rencontreront à Abou Dhabi, aux Émirats arabes unis, les 10 et 11 novembre pour un nouveau cycle de discussions. Les États-Unis seront représentés par Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner, et quatre pays européens (la France, le Royaume-Uni, l’Allemagne et l’Italie) seront également présents à Abou Dhabi par l’intermédiaire de leurs conseillers à la sécurité nationale, en plus de représentants de l’OTAN et de l’Union. La composition des équipes de négociateurs russes et ukrainiens est une variable clef pour saisir les intentions du Kremlin. En confiant depuis 2022 la direction de ses délégations à un idéologue ou à un militaire plutôt qu’à un diplomate, Poutine signale qu’il n’envisage pas de mettre fin à la guerre. La délégation qui sera présente à Abou Dhabi à partir de demain, mardi 10, reprend pour l’essentiel celle du dernier cycle, à Genève en février. Elle sera de nouveau dirigée par Vladimir Medinsky, qui prend part depuis 2022 aux négociations entre la Russie et l’Ukraine. Medinsky, conseiller de Vladimir Poutine, est un idéologue qui avait profité de précédentes négociations pour faire de longues leçons sur les « causes profondes » du conflit, selon des sources ukrainiennes et américaines Война Тысяча четыреста сорок второй день. В Абу-Даби начался новый раунд трехсторонних переговоров (там « пресса не предусмотрена »). В Белгороде — блэкаут из-за удара ВСУ », Meduza , 4 février 2026.'> 6 . Il sera accompagné d’Igor Kostioukov, le chef du renseignement militaire (GRU) qui avait mené les cycles de janvier et février à Abou Dhabi, et du vice-ministre des Affaires étrangères Mikhaïl Galouzine. Le vice-ministre des Affaires étrangères Sergueï Riabkov, chargé des relations avec les Amériques, du contrôle des armements et du dossier nucléaire iranien, devrait faire officiellement partie de la délégation pour la première fois. Iouri Jigarlovski, chef adjoint de la Direction principale des opérations de l’état-major général, chargée de la planification et de la conduite des opérations militaires, devrait quant à lui représenter l’état-major aux côtés de Kostioukov. Lors des cycles d’Istanbul, en 2025, le ministère de la Défense était représenté par Alexandre Fomine, alors vice-ministre de la Défense, qui siégeait déjà aux négociations de 2022. Il a quitté le ministère en octobre 2025 et a été remplacé à son poste par Vassili Osmakov. La composition de la délégation russe, si elle présente quelques changements, ne laisse pas entrevoir de changement dans la position de Moscou. Riabkov a en effet été l’un des principaux artisans des ultimatums adressés aux États-Unis et aux membres de l’OTAN en 2021, qui revenaient, selon l’Institute for the Study of War, à démanteler l’Alliance sous couvert de « garanties de sécurité » pour la Russie Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 7, 2026 , Institute for the Study of War.'> 7 . Medinsky, le chef de la délégation, a quant à lui piloté la nouvelle collection de manuels d’histoire, généralisée en septembre 2026 à toutes les écoles russes, qui présente aux élèves les « héros » de la guerre en Ukraine qu’ils doivent connaître pour réussir l’examen d’histoire Государство обязано донести до учеников свою точку зрения », Kommersant , 21 mars 2026.'> 8 . L’article Négociations Ukraine-Russie à Abou Dhabi : que révèle la composition de la délégation russe ? est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: 2027: Why we’re yet to print over 2.9m PVCs — INEC
items.description: ….Removes 1,609,553 multiple, deceased registrants ….Identifies 54 staff responsible for multiple registration, unusual registration patterns, substituted photos ….Yet to receive CTC of judgment on Atiku/ADC By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has explained why those who registered in the third phase of its Continuous Voter Registration CVR are yet to have their Permanent Voter Cards even as it announced a massive purge of the national voter register ahead of the 2027 general elections. Addressing a press conference in Abuja, the INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Ojo Amupitan, SAN, disclosed that the commission has successfully removed 1,609,553 invalid and deceased records from the system. “The Commission recognises that the detection of irregularities raises legitimate questions about how they arose. The response is evidence-led investigation, completed corrective action and stronger preventive controls. “1,609,553 records have been removed, comprising 1,608,660 confirmed invalid registrations and 873 verified deceased-voter records. INEC will continue to communicate verifiable aggregate outcomes while protecting personal information and the integrity of ongoing investigations”, said Amupitan. Addressing reporters regarding the status of unprinted cards, the INEC Chairman stated: “The distribution of Phases 1 and 2 of the PVC and transferred PVCs is on-going at the various LGAs in Nigeria. Some of the PVC for the third and final Phase are being delivered and they would be dispatched to the States by next week. “Meanwhile as from 1st December 2026, distribution will go back to the Registration Areas all over Nigeria. We appeal to those that registered in the third phase to be a little bit patient since the production is done outside the country”. Vanguard recalls that those who registered in total in the third phase were 2,970,257 before the commission’s de-duplication protocol. The sweeping clean-up of the register followed widespread public outcry and intense scrutiny over anomalies spotted on the preliminary register displayed between October 9 and 15, 2026. A rigorous technical audit utilizing the Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) uncovered systemic manipulations, including unusual registration patterns, substituted photographs, and fraudulent multiple registrations. Crucially, the investigation indicted internal personnel who abused their offices. Prof. Amupitan revealed that the commission identified 54 staff members cutting across 10 states who deliberately bypassed standard operating procedures and exploited special provisions meant for vulnerable citizens, such as persons with disabilities. Disciplinary actions and possible prosecutions have been initiated against the culprits. Reacting to media inquiries surrounding court cases involving political actors, the INEC Chairman maintained that the electoral umpire operates strictly on authenticated legal instruments rather than speculative reports. “On ADC/Atiku: as of today, we have not received the Certified True Copy of the court judgment and we don’t act based on what we see on the social media”, he said. INEC noted that while the recent 2025/2026 CVR clean-up resolved immediate anomalies, historical data carried over from 2011 to 2023 continues to present legacy duplications. Consequently, the commission’s board has directed that flagged entries from past cycles be expunged after verification. To further safeguard the integrity of the upcoming 2027 polls, INEC assured the public that robust mechanisms—including the mandatory physical presence of voters and biometric authentication via the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) using fingerprints or facial recognition—remain firmly in place to prevent multiple voting and unauthorized accreditation. items.title: Maroc ou Pays-Bas : Xavi affiche son respect pour les choix des binationaux
items.description: Le sélectionneur des Pays-Bas, Xavi Hernandez, a assuré ce lundi qu’il respectait les choix internationaux des joueurs d’origine marocaine, tout en se disant disposé à échanger avec eux lorsque cela s’avère nécessaire. Interrogé lors d’une conférence de presse sur le débat qui agite actuellement les Pays-Bas autour du choix de plusieurs jeunes joueurs d’origine marocaine de représenter le Maroc, Xavi a adopté une position claire : le choix des joueurs doit être respecté. Le technicien néerlandais a notamment été interrogé sur plusieurs talents ayant récemment rejoint le projet de la sélection marocaine, parmi lesquels Abdellah Ouazane et Ayoub Ouakfir. « Je pense que cela relève de la Fédération, c’est elle qui doit en parler » , a déclaré Xavi, avant d’ajouter : « Je respecte les joueurs et je respecte leurs décisions. Bien entendu, je peux intervenir et parler avec les joueurs si cela est nécessaire pour les impliquer. » La conférence de presse a également abordé le cas de Lamine Yamal, qui était éligible pour représenter le Maroc avant de choisir de porter le maillot de l’Espagne. Interrogé sur l’existence d’un débat similaire en Espagne autour de ce choix, Xavi a estimé que la situation n’avait pas suscité de discussion comparable. Pour le sélectionneur néerlandais, la décision de Lamine Yamal de représenter l’Espagne relevait avant tout d’un choix personnel, qui avait été respecté. The post Maroc ou Pays-Bas : Xavi affiche son respect pour les choix des binationaux appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Nine Zimbabweans caught allegedly trying to leave South Africa to fight in Ukraine
items.description: Nine Zimbabweans have been arrested in South Africa after they were caught allegedly trying to leave the country to fight in the war between Russia and the Ukraine, police say. The group, aged between 20 and 26, were arrested in and around Johannesburg by a multidisciplinary team on Sunday evening. They were caught as they were “preparing to board flights out of the country”, authorities added, but their final destination is unclear. They have been charged with contravening South Africa’s Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act, which outlaws mercenary activity without government permission. Police said five people were arrested at South Africa’s biggest airport, OR Tambo, and another four at a hotel in Bruma, east of Johannesburg by a multidisciplinary team that involved Interpol. All nine later appeared in court, according to state prosecutors. The police statement added that the involvement of Interpol and other international law enforcement agencies indicated that the suspects had also allegedly violated laws in their respective home countries, prompting cooperation with South African authorities. They have also not said whether the group allegedly intended to fight for Russia or Ukraine nor provided details of the organisations allegedly involved in facilitating their travel. Citizens of several African countries, including Kenya, Ghana and South Africa, have gone to fight for Russia in Ukraine – some they had been duped and had not realised where they were going. A Ukrainian intelligence assessment estimated earlier this year that more than 1,700 people from 36 countries in Africa have been recruited to fight for Russia. Kenya at the time estimated that 252 citizens had been illegally conscripted in Russia. In March, Foreign Minister Musalia Mudavadi visited Moscow to address the issue. He said at the time that an agreement had been reached to stop recruiting Kenyan nationals. In March, Zimbabwe said that 15 of its nationals had been killed after being recruited to fight for Russia in Ukraine, with more than 60 still trapped on the frontlines. The previous month, South Africa secured the return of 17 South Africans who were allegedly tricked into joining the war. In December last year, South African authorities arrested five people, including a journalist, for allegedly recruiting people to join the war. Ukraine has also been recruiting foreign nationals, including from Africa.

items.title: TenTrade brings financial market experts together to promote trading education in Lagos
items.description: Financial services company, TenTrade, has brought together financial market experts, traders and industry stakeholders in Lagos to discuss ways of expanding participation in financial markets and preparing the next generation of traders. The gathering, held in Ikeja on Saturday, November 7, 2026, was themed, “One Community, One Future: Building the Next Generation of Traders.” The event featured discussions on financial market education, trading opportunities and the future of the trading industry in Africa. Speaking at the event, Wilfred Obasi, Regional Director for Africa at TenTrade, identified impatience and the desire to make quick money as major challenges confronting young traders. “For young traders, they are not patient enough. People want to make quick money. It is why we are making the event work today to enlighten young traders,” Obasi said. He explained that the event was organised to expose young people to the realities of financial trading and help them develop the patience and knowledge required to navigate the market. Obasi also spoke about the company’s international expansion, noting that TenTrade had grown from operating in one or two regions to having a presence in about 30 countries, including Kenya, Ghana, Nigeria and Indonesia. He attributed the company’s growth to its emphasis on building trust and empowering clients. “We make sure that we do not overpromise. We empower our clients and we do well for them,” he said. Also speaking, Ademola Adeagbo, Head of Education at TenTrade Africa, urged traders to prioritise risk management, discipline and trading psychology to achieve consistency in the financial markets. He identified fear, greed, fear of missing out (FOMO) and revenge trading as common emotional traps that could undermine trading decisions and expose traders to losses. Adeagbo stressed that traders must develop the discipline to manage risks and avoid making decisions based on emotions. Similarly, Kehinde Shogeke, TenTrade’s Sales Team Lead, said traders needed adequate market knowledge, sufficient capital and discipline to improve their chances of navigating the financial markets. He observed that many people entered forex trading without understanding its fundamentals, viewing it instead as an opportunity to make quick money. “Most traders or new traders see forex as a get-rich-quickly scheme. There is a basic knowledge of the market that they must have. Have a good knowledge, capital and discipline,” he said. Shogeke further explained that TenTrade offered different account options to accommodate traders with varying needs, including regular brokerage and funded accounts. According to him, the company’s regular brokerage offering provides up to six types of accounts, while its equity account allows traders to access up to $500,000. He described the combination of brokerage and funded trading accounts as one of the company’s distinctive offerings. Meanwhile, a TenTrade partner, Peace Ohikhena, said her relationship with the company had helped her establish a forex trading community with more than 2,000 members. “My experience has been great. Apart from being a trader, I am also a partner. My partnership with TenTrade has helped me to build my own community of traders because I own a forex community currently of over 2,000 members,” she said. Ohikhena, who travelled from Port Harcourt to attend the Lagos event, described the opportunity to learn and interact with other participants as worthwhile. “My journey down to Lagos from Port Harcourt for this event is worth it. I am someone who is always open to learn and I am glad I did this,” she added. Similarly, Lilian Aniche, TenTrade’s Business Development and Partnership Manager, who said she joined the company about four months ago, described her experience as exciting, identifying its people and support system as factors that distinguished it from other platforms. “I recently joined TT about four months ago, and it’s been an exciting experience so far. What’s sets TT is its people. It is easy to get products but what makes the entire products of TT different is its people,” she said. TenTrade operates under Evalanch Ltd, which is licensed and regulated by the Seychelles Financial Services Authority (FSA), with licence number SD082. The company’s website also warns that trading contracts for difference (CFDs), including forex, involves significant risks and could result in the loss of an investor’s entire investment. The post TenTrade brings financial market experts together to promote trading education in Lagos appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nasarawa APC protests alleged violence, SDP alleges bias
items.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia Members and supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Nasarawa State on Monday staged a protest in Lafia over alleged political violence, intimidation of party members and the disruption of the party’s presidential rally attended by Vice President Kashim Shettima. Addressing journalists and security officials during the demonstration, the state APC Chairman, Dr. Aliyu Bello, called for investigations into reported attacks on party supporters, including the alleged killing of a supporter in the Tudun Wada area of Lafia. Bello expressed concern over what he described as the failure of law enforcement agencies to act on complaints previously submitted by the party. He said the protest was organised to demand justice and adequate protection for party members, insisting that the APC remained committed to peaceful political activities. “We came here to demand justice that a full-scale investigation be carried out and the perpetrators of these acts arrested and prosecuted,” he said. The APC chairman also raised concerns about alleged threats and conduct by some opposition figures, calling on security agencies to ensure that all political actors operate within the law. Responding on behalf of Governor Abdullahi Sule, the Deputy Governor, Dr Emmanuel Akabe, described the reported incidents as a matter of concern and criticised the security arrangements surrounding the disruption of the Vice-President’s rally. Akabe said security agencies had been briefed ahead of Shettima’s visit and stressed that protecting lives and property remained their responsibility. “It is unfortunate because the responsibility of security men is to protect lives and property. If you cannot protect individuals in your state, then a lot needs to be answered,” he said. The deputy governor disclosed that the State Emergency Security Council had convened to consider measures to prevent further disturbances. He assured the protesters that the state government would support efforts to ensure that anyone found culpable was dealt with in accordance with the law. Speaking on behalf of the Nasarawa State Police Command, Assistant Commissioner of Police Gaya Ahmed reaffirmed the neutrality of security agencies and their commitment to investigating complaints. “The IGP has made it clear that the police are neutral, and we keep on maintaining that neutrality,” Ahmed said. He assured the protesters that petitions submitted by the APC would be forwarded to the incoming Commissioner of Police for investigation. A representative of the Department of State Services (DSS), the Deputy Director of Administration, also acknowledged receipt of the party’s complaints and commended the protesters for conducting themselves peacefully without obstructing public roads. However, the Nasarawa State chapter of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) criticised the demonstration, accusing the state government and the APC of using the protest to target opposition figures. In a statement, the Director of Digital Media and Communications for the Muhammad Adamu Abubakar Campaign Council, High Chief Otaru Douglas, described the demonstration as an attempt to portray the opposition as responsible for the state’s security challenges. The SDP said its governorship candidate and campaign council opposed what it described as a state-sponsored protest against opposition stakeholders. “We have taken note of all the inciting and provocative rhetoric coming from the APC and its leadership through their white-garment cult-like movement, which is rather unfortunate and unpatriotic of the government and those involved in the protest,” the statement said. The opposition party argued that the government should prioritise dialogue and conflict resolution rather than actions it said could heighten political tension. It maintained that the government had a responsibility to provide a level playing field for all political parties, protect citizens and guarantee their constitutional right to peaceful assembly. The SDP also warned that protests should not become instruments of political confrontation, urging the state government to engage opposition parties and allow security agencies to carry out their duties impartially. The party further called on the government to avoid actions that could deepen political divisions, stressing that Nasarawa State needed peace, justice and constructive engagement among political stakeholders. The exchange comes amid heightened political activities in Nasarawa State ahead of the 2027 general elections, with both parties expressing concerns over security and political conduct. items.title: How Ghana can build an economy that produces more with her abundant resources
items.description: In September 2026, it took me more than twelve hours to travel the 266 kilometres from Nkroful to Kumasi through the important mining towns of Tarkwa, Bogosu, Dunkwa-on-Offin, Ayanfuri and Obuasi. In 2025, I compared Accra–Kumasi trips of at least six hours with a three-hour journey from Abidjan to Yamoussoukro over a similar distance. These were individual journeys, but they raise a question for every producer who depends on a road. How much of a working day can you afford to lose getting goods to market? The World Bank reported that Ghana’s economy grew by 6 per cent in 2025, yet only 13 per cent of workers aged 15 to 64 held formal wage or high-skilled jobs in 2023, down from 15 per cent in 2012. Better infrastructure can help farms and firms turn growth into more productive jobs. Roads and electricity networks show why public ownership matters to productivity and welfare. They serve households and businesses across whole regions, including places where the commercial return alone may be too low to justify investment. Government must define what the public should receive from these assets, fund those obligations openly and give Parliament and citizens the information they need to hold operators to account. What citizens should get from public ownership ? Public ownership makes sense where duplicating a network would be wasteful or where essential services would otherwise be undersupplied. An electricity transmission grid is a case in point. For households and firms, the benefits should be visible in wider access, fewer outages and reliable service at a sustainable cost. Utilities should publish these results alongside audited accounts and disclose the cost and funding of any subsidised service. That lets Parliament distinguish the cost of a public obligation from losses caused by poor management. The 2026 Budget proposed a 1,200-megawatt state-owned thermal plant. Before committing public funds, government should compare its lifetime cost and expected reliability with rehabilitating existing plants and procuring power from other sources. It should disclose any guarantees taxpayers may have to honour. The same accountability should apply to support for private firms. Publish the beneficiaries, the cost and the expected gains in output and sustained jobs. What the CRC proposed and what government decided The Constitution Review Committee proposed amending Chapter 14 to give the State Interests and Governance Authority (SIGA) constitutional status and make it accountable to Parliament for its independent oversight of state enterprises and state-controlled joint ventures. It proposed merit-based board appointments, barring ministers, deputy ministers and MPs from boards and management, and giving properly constituted boards authority to appoint, supervise and remove chief executives and senior managers. It also proposed public disclosure of audited annual accounts, with sanctions for failures to comply. In its July 2026 position paper, the government rejected constitutional status for SIGA. It argued that Parliament already has the power to establish and regulate such bodies and that no institutional vulnerability had been demonstrated to justify elevation. On the proposed rules to depoliticise enterprise governance, the government favoured legislation so appointment procedures, governance standards and directors’ duties could be updated as needed. I would put SIGA’s independence and duty to report to Parliament and the public in the Constitution, with fixed terms for its leaders and removal on defined grounds after a fair process. Legislation can specify how vacancies are advertised, candidates assessed and directors held to their duties. Government should set ownership policy, boards should run enterprises through their executives, and SIGA should independently assess what they deliver. At SIGA’s September 2026 conference, President Mahama reported that only 61 entities in the wider state portfolio submitted audited accounts by the statutory deadline, and only 72 of 148 chief executives signed performance contracts. SIGA should publish an enterprise-by-enterprise record of missed deadlines, verified results and corrective action. Parliament should call boards to explain repeated failures, including what they mean for the people who rely on their services. Clear the road bottlenecks that hold back production Unfinished works, damaged surfaces and stranded trucks on major highways make journey times unpredictable. A truck that spends the day in traffic completes fewer trips. A processor may miss a shipment or tie up cash holding extra stock, and perishable goods can lose value before reaching market. Government should prioritise repairs and completion of works by the delays they impose on entire freight corridors and publish journey times and their variability. Ghana suspended a mandatory towing levy in 2017 after objections to the fee and contracting arrangements. A pay-after-towing approach was subsequently announced. The National Road Safety Authority told the Daily Graphic it planned to start a new system in January 2027 based on private towing subscriptions or insurance cover. On major routes such as the N1 and N5, recovery vehicles should be stationed near known bottlenecks. Dispatch should begin when a hazard is reported, billing disputes should be settled after the lane is clear, and the authority should publish actual clearance times against its standards. Make heavy freight pay its share Ghana should calculate the cost of routine maintenance and resurfacing, then set heavy-vehicle tolls by axle class and corridor use. Côte d’Ivoire published a CFA 5,000 charge for vehicles with three or more axles at Attinguié and Singrobo in February 2025. Togo announced CFA 2,800 for trucks with three to five axles from July 2026. These are charges per toll point. Compare the total charge for equivalent port-to-border journeys before setting rates. Parliament authorised an electronic tolling concession in July 2026. Government should publish the tariffs, collection costs, the state’s share and how much maintenance the proceeds will fund. Underpricing heavy road use can leave taxpayers covering part of the cost of transit freight from the Sahel. The same rates and axle-load limits should be applied to comparable domestic and foreign trucks, while accounting for existing road-user charges and showing which repairs the tolls pay for. Connect farms to markets and protect investment My earlier research documented the limits imposed by dependence on rainfall, limited technology and weak investment. Farmer Service Centres should coordinate machinery hire with irrigation, storage and buyers in the same production areas, publish their charges and booking rules, and assess results after two crop seasons. Resolve competing land claims before investing, with customary authorities, tenants and other users involved. Producers also need independent courts that enforce contracts. A processor waiting to recover a debt may run out of cash to buy the next crop. Commercial and land courts should pilot early case conferences, record reasons for adjournments, and publish the time cases take to reach judgment and enforcement. Graphic Online reported that during the 2026 Kwahu Easter Business Forum, President Mahama said he resisted pressure to exclude capable firms perceived to be close to the opposition. The IMF’s Ghana Governance Diagnostic warns that cancelling contracts or leaving them unpaid after elections can generate costly claims. Incoming governments should review inherited contracts against legality, performance and value for money, publish reasons for cancellation and assess potential judgment debts before acting. Firms are more likely to buy equipment and train workers when contracts can survive a change of government. The way forward for a productive economy Ghana can turn its abundant resources into better jobs by making roads and power reliable and contracts enforceable. Public ownership should widen access to essential services and show citizens what their money buys. Start where freight delays cost producers most. Finish critical works, deploy recovery crews and publish journey times and toll-funded repairs. Protect SIGA’s independence and have Parliament scrutinise audited accounts and service results. Link farm support to buyers, speed up contract enforcement and apply published criteria to inherited contracts. Measure progress in service reliability, output and jobs.

items.description: La cavalière Eden Kazoum a bien décroché le bronze en saut d'obstacles par équipes aux JOJ Dakar 2026. Mais cette médaille, remportée avec la Team Afrique, ne figure pas au compteur officiel du Sénégal. Le 5 novembre, au Centre équestre de Diamniadio, Eden Kazoum est montée sur la troisième marche du podium de l'épreuve de saut d'obstacles par équipes. Une performance saluée dans la presse et sur les réseaux sociaux, où beaucoup l'ont ajoutée au bilan de la délégation sénégalaise. À tort, si l'on s'en tient au tableau officiel des médailles. Tout tient à la composition de l'équipe. La jeune Sénégalaise ne concourait pas sous les couleurs nationales, mais au sein de la Team Afrique, aux côtés du Sud-Africain Bo Reed, de l'Égyptien Yassin El Bassiuony et du Marocain Ghali Bougja. Aux Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse, l'équitation fonctionne ainsi : chaque pays qualifié n'aligne qu'un cavalier, et les cavaliers sont regroupés en équipes continentales. Ils ne montent même pas leurs propres chevaux, attribués par tirage au sort. Une ligne à part au tableau Or le Comité international olympique (CIO) ne répartit pas entre les pays les médailles d'une équipe formée d'athlètes de plusieurs nations. Ces équipes dites « mixtes » sont enregistrées sous un code spécifique, MIX, et leurs médailles sont comptabilisées séparément, hors des bilans nationaux. Lors de la cérémonie protocolaire, c'est d'ailleurs le drapeau olympique qui est hissé. Cette pratique a cours aux JOJ depuis la première édition, à Singapour en 2010. Le tableau publié ce lundi 9 novembre sur le site officiel des Jeux le confirme. Après 101 épreuves sur 151, le Sénégal y occupe la 6e place avec 7 médailles : 4 en or et 3 en bronze. Les titres sont l'œuvre des lutteurs de plage Elisabeth Diatta (55 kg), Maguette Diop (80 kg) et Ndeye Khady Anna Diatta (45 kg), ainsi que des Lionceaux du basket 3×3. Les bronzes reviennent au judoka Matar Diop (-66 kg), au lutteur Ablaye Diouf (90 kg) et aux Lioncelles du basket 3×3, médaillées ce lundi. Aucune médaille d'équitation n'apparaît sur la fiche de la délégation. Pas de rattrapage en individuel Eden Kazoum, championne du Sénégal junior en 2025 et unique représentante du pays en équitation, avait une seconde chance de rapporter une médaille comptabilisée pour le Sénégal : la finale individuelle, le 6 novembre. Elle y a écopé de 14 points de pénalité, dont 6 pour dépassement du temps, et a terminé loin du podium. Le titre est revenu au Suisse Mike Smits. Son bronze reste une médaille olympique de la jeunesse à part entière, inscrite à son palmarès personnel. Mais présenter le bilan du Sénégal à 8 médailles, en y ajoutant ce podium continental, est inexact. Abdou Khadir SECK

items.title: Religious leaders have a key role in El Niño preparedness – NADMO
items.description: The National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) has called on religious leaders to play a leading role in educating communities and preparing households for the possible effects of the developing El Niño weather phenomenon. Deputy Director of NADMO for the Korle Klottey Municipal Assembly, Esenam Adzo Norgey Apawu, says the influence of churches, mosques and their leaders gives them an important platform to communicate early warnings and help families take preventive action. “Religious leaders have a strong influence in their communities. This gives them an important role in educating people about El Niño, sharing early warnings and helping families prepare for its possible effects,” she said. She stressed that information on the weather phenomenon should go beyond government offices and conference rooms to reach people in their homes and communities, where preparedness measures are most needed. “Information about El Niño must not remain in offices and meeting rooms. It must reach ordinary people in their homes and communities, where preparedness begins,” she added. Mrs Apawu was speaking at a breakfast meeting organised by GreenFaith Ghana as part of efforts to strengthen the capacity of religious leaders and places of worship to anticipate, prepare for and respond to risks associated with the El Niño event. She said preparing for the possible impacts of the phenomenon should not be left to government institutions alone, urging religious leaders, traditional authorities and community members to contribute to local preparedness efforts. “Preparing for El Niño should not be left to government institutions alone. Religious leaders, traditional authorities and community members all have a role to play,” she said. The Ghana Meteorological Agency has warned of a very strong and intensifying El Niño, which could result in hotter, drier and dustier conditions during the dry season, with possible implications for agriculture, water resources, energy supply and public health. The forecast points to heightened heat stress, particularly in northern Ghana, between February and April 2027, while sudden heavy rainfall and localised flooding could still occur in parts of the south. The initiative seeks to make religious institutions part of community-level preparedness and response efforts as Ghana prepares for the potential effects of the weather event. GMet Deputy Director of Research and Applied Meteorology, Francisca Martey Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMet) Deputy Director of Research and Applied Meteorology, Francisca Martey, said the agency’s assessment points to a very strong and intensifying El Niño, which is expected to bring hotter, drier and dustier conditions from late November. She warned that heat stress could peak between February and April 2027, particularly in northern Ghana, while parts of the south could still experience sudden heavy rainfall and localised flooding. She said the conditions could affect agriculture, water resources, energy generation and public health.

items.title: EOCO says visit to Wontumi’s property was for valuation, not a raid
items.description: The Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) has denied reports that its officers ransacked a property belonging to the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) Ashanti Regional Chairman, Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi. In a statement issued on Monday, November 9, 2026, the Office said its officers, accompanied by officials from the Lands Commission, visited the Tema property to take coordinates and measurements for a professional valuation. EOCO said the exercise formed part of due process following the freezing of the property, which it said was confirmed by a court last year. “The said property was frozen by EOCO and confirmed by the Court last year. As part of due process, EOCO and Lands Commission officials were at the property to pick the coordinates and measurements to enable Lands Commission to conduct a professional valuation,” the statement said. The Office said the activity was completed in less than 10 minutes and that no incident occurred during the visit. “This is what has been characterised as ransacking of Wontumi’s house,” the statement said. EOCO rejected the reports circulating in the media and urged the public not to rely on what it described as false publications about the exercise. “EOCO urges the general public to disregard false publications circulating within the media space about the said activity,” it added. The property was frozen by EOCO as part of an ongoing investigation, with the action reportedly confirmed by a court last year. Monday’s visit was intended to provide the Lands Commission with the measurements and coordinates required to conduct a professional valuation of the property. items.title: Santé mentale des étudiants : Al Akhawayn University, chef de file africain d’une IA responsable
items.description: L'Université Al Akhawayn à Ifrane (AUI) a accueilli l’initiative «Building Inclusive, AI-Enabled Mental Health Support Ecosystems in African Universities ». Elle a réuni des universités du réseau AFRETEC (African Engineering and Technology Network), un réseau panafricain d'universités technologiques dont Al Akhawayn est le premier membre d'Afrique du Nord. Les échanges portaient sur un projet pilote conçu et porté par l'AUI en collaboration avec AFRETEC. Ce projet associe l'accompagnement humain à un outil d'intelligence artificielle responsable, au service du bien-être et de la santé mentale des étudiants. Testé et enrichi par les universités partenaires, le modèle pourra désormais être adapté et repris sur d'autres campus africains. Al Akhawayn University, à l'avant-garde d'une initiative panafricaine Le workshop s'inscrit dans le pilier Inclusion d'AFRETEC. L'AUI en est l'institution cheffe de file. Il répond à des défis majeurs pour l'enseignement supérieur africain : la stigmatisation encore attachée à la santé mentale ; l'accès limité aux ressources d'accompagnement ; les besoins spécifiques des étudiants sous-représentés ou en situation de vulnérabilité. Son ambition est de bâtir une communauté de soutien durable, fondée sur l'inclusion, l'équité et la diversité. Elle s'appuie sur des réseaux de soutien entre pairs, des espaces d'écoute sûrs et bienveillants, et des ressources innovantes, dont des outils d'IA. À Ifrane, plusieurs participants se sont réunis : coordinateurs AFRETEC, dirigeants universitaires, responsables des affaires étudiantes, conseillers, spécialistes de l'inclusion et du soutien entre pairs, et experts en IA et en données. Ils venaient de l'Université du Witwatersrand (Afrique du Sud), de l'American University in Cairo (Égypte), de l'Université de Nairobi (Kenya), de l'Université Agostinho Neto (Angola), de l'Université Cheikh Anta Diop (Sénégal), de l'Université de Lagos (Nigeria) et de l'Université du Rwanda. L'analyse des besoins et l'outil d'IA développés par l'AUI ont servi de base à l'ensemble des travaux. Le partenariat est ainsi passé de la présentation d'un projet à la conception et à la planification communes de sa mise en œuvre. En accueillant cet atelier pour l'ensemble du réseau, Al Akhawayn s'affirme comme une référence africaine en matière de bien-être étudiant, et pas seulement comme un contributeur technologique. Co-construire un modèle commun Des ateliers thématiques de co-conception ont abouti à une feuille de route commune. Les participants ont retenu un modèle d'écosystème de soutien plutôt qu'un service isolé. Ce modèle relie les dimensions académique, sociale, physique et numérique, ainsi que l'orientation vers des professionnels. Il repose sur un socle commun de principes : confidentialité, supervision humaine, procédures claires d'orientation, accessibilité et collecte de données limitée au strict nécessaire. Chaque université peut ensuite l'adapter à son contexte, qu'il s'agisse des équipes, de la langue, de l'aménagement des espaces ou des technologies. L'inclusion fait partie du cahier des charges dès la conception : communication multilingue, accessibilité pour les personnes en situation de handicap, respect de la vie privée, sensibilité culturelle et options adaptées aux connexions limitées ou hors ligne. Une intelligence artificielle responsable, au service de l'humain L'outil développé par l'AUI repose sur un principe clair : la relation humaine reste le fondement de l'accompagnement. L'IA aide les étudiants à trouver leur chemin vers les bons services, facilite un premier contact, fournit de l'information et oriente vers les bons interlocuteurs. En revanche, elle ne pose jamais de diagnostic, ne remplace pas les professionnels de santé et ne fonctionne jamais sans supervision humaine. Les universités partenaires l'ont testée et ont confirmé son potentiel comme porte d'entrée simple et outil de coordination. L'outil a ainsi été évalué par l'ensemble d'un réseau, et non plus seulement en interne. Le campus d'Al Akhawayn, terrain d'expérimentation À Al Akhawayn University, le projet est dirigé avec l'appui de l'Office of Academic Research (OAR), le bureau de la recherche académique de l'Université. L'OAR accompagne la conception, le développement et la gestion des projets de recherche et des partenariats scientifiques de l'AUI. Les prochaines étapes à l'AUI sont les suivantes : cartographier les parcours d'accès des étudiants aux services de soutien ; faire de la Wellness Room la porte d'entrée d'un dispositif de soutien élargi, former les enseignants, les personnels et les étudiants engagés dans le soutien entre pairs à repérer les besoins, réagir et orienter, sans se substituer aux professionnels ; renforcer l'outil d'IA avec une supervision humaine accrue, une collecte de données réduite et des protocoles de crise clairement définis, assurer un suivi de l'accès et de l'orientation des étudiants, sans aucune logique de surveillance, tester l'ensemble avec des étudiants et les membres du personnel avant le déploiement complet. Une démarche ancrée dans la philosophie des liberal arts Cette initiative reflète le modèle éducatif d'Al Akhawayn, fondé sur les liberal arts : accompagner chaque étudiant dans ses apprentissages comme dans son développement personnel. En partageant son expérience avec ses partenaires africains, l'Université contribue à une coopération où l'innovation part des besoins réels des étudiants et s'enrichit de l'expérience de chaque établissement. À propos d'AFRETEC L'African Engineering and Technology Network (AFRETEC) est un réseau panafricain d'universités technologiques. Il a pour mission de favoriser une transformation numérique inclusive du continent, en s'appuyant sur l'enseignement supérieur et la collaboration. Le réseau intervient dans trois domaines : l'enseignement et l'apprentissage, la création de connaissances et l'entrepreneuriat. Il rassemble notamment Carnegie Mellon University Africa (Rwanda), l'American University in Cairo (Égypte), l'Université du Witwatersrand (Afrique du Sud), l'Université de Nairobi (Kenya), l'Université Cheikh Anta Diop (Sénégal), l'Université du Rwanda, l'Université de Lagos (Nigeria), l'Université Agostinho Neto (Angola) et l'Université Al Akhawayn à Ifrane, première université d'Afrique du Nord membre du réseau. The post Santé mentale des étudiants : Al Akhawayn University, chef de file africain d’une IA responsable appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Ghana’s 2027 Budget: Three important policy questions about the New Economy
items.description: Introduction On November 12, 2026, Ghana’s Minister for Finance, Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson, is expected to present the 2027 Budget, which the government is promoting as the beginning of a New Economy. At the centre of this agenda is a proposed US$10 billion investment programme over four years, targeting infrastructure, agriculture, manufacturing and other productive sectors. The shift from macroeconomic stabilisation toward investment-led growth is a welcome policy direction. Having made significant progress in restoring macroeconomic stability, Ghana now has an opportunity to build on these gains by addressing structural constraints to economic growth, expanding productive capacity, creating sustainable employment and improving household incomes. However, the proposed New Economy raises three important economic policy questions: How much of the announced investment is genuinely new? How will the government finance the larger fiscal deficit? And how will the investment programme be reconciled with the government’s ambitious foreign reserve accumulation strategy? These questions deserve careful consideration ahead of the budget presentation. 1. How Much of the New Economy Investment Is Genuinely New? The government intends to reduce its primary surplus target from 1.5% of GDP to 0.5% in 2027, creating additional fiscal space equivalent to approximately 1% of GDP. Preliminary announcements also suggest additional revenue mobilisation of 0.5% of GDP, potentially increasing total fiscal space by 1.5 percentage points. However, the 2026 Budget had already projected capital expenditure of 4.6% of GDP for 2027, a level arguably inadequate for an economy facing significant infrastructure deficits and an urgent need for productive investment. The critical question is therefore how much additional investment the New Economy will deliver beyond this already modest allocation. With the announcement of the New Economy, it is important to establish whether the proposed investment programme will increase this allocation or largely finance projects already included in the government’s existing expenditure plans. If the entire additional fiscal space were allocated to capital expenditure, the public investment-to-GDP ratio could theoretically increase from 4.6% to 6.1%. The critical question is whether the forthcoming budget will deliver an increase of this magnitude or whether the New Economy will largely incorporate projects already included under the Big Push Infrastructure Programme, the 24-Hour Economy initiative and other existing commitments. If the government is genuinely committed to investment-led growth, the minimum expectation should be that the entire additional fiscal space of 1.5% of GDP is channelled into growth-enhancing expenditure, with an increase in capital expenditure from 4.6% to approximately 6.1% of GDP providing a measurable benchmark. The ultimate test, however, is whether this additional spending expands productive capacity, stimulates private investment and creates sustainable employment. 2. How Will the Government Finance the Larger Fiscal Deficit? A reduction in the primary surplus from 1.5% to 0.5% of GDP would, holding other fiscal aggregates constant, increase the overall cash deficit from approximately 2.5% to 3.5% of GDP. This raises an important financing question, particularly because Ghana has substantial debt repayment obligations and the government has indicated that it does not intend to return to the international Eurobond market. The 2026 budget already envisaged substantial reliance on domestic borrowing in 2027, partly because external debt amortisation was expected to exceed new external disbursements. With the government ruling out Eurobond issuance, additional fiscal financing would likely have to come primarily from the domestic financial market. Under these assumptions, net domestic financing would increase from GH¢72.5 billion to approximately GH¢90.6 billion, an increase of nearly 25%. This does not necessarily pose an immediate threat to debt sustainability. The IMF’s July 2026 assessment upgraded Ghana’s debt-distress risk to moderate and projected public debt at approximately 54.9% of GDP in 2027, under a framework incorporating the revised primary surplus target. The more immediate question is whether the domestic financial market can accommodate the additional borrowing without undermining the recovery in private-sector credit The Bank of Ghana’s September 2026 Monetary Policy Report reveals encouraging developments. By August 2026, private-sector credit was growing at 35.5% in nominal terms and 29% in real terms, compared with 13.3% and 1.7%, respectively, a year earlier. Average lending rates had declined from 24.2% to 15.9%, while banking-sector liquidity remained comfortable. These developments suggest improving financing conditions for private investment. However, the government’s increased domestic borrowing requirement could compete with this recovery, particularly as private-sector credit demand strengthens. Although domestic liquidity conditions are currently favourable, the Bank of Ghana reports limited activity in longer-term government securities, raising questions about the maturity structure and cost of additional borrowing. The 2027 Budget must therefore provide a credible domestic financing strategy that demonstrates how the government intends to accommodate higher borrowing while preserving affordable credit for private investment. After all, an investment-led growth strategy would risk undermining its own objectives if increased public borrowing significantly crowded out the private investment it seeks to stimulate. 3. The New Economy and GANRAP: A Potential Policy Trade-Off The third question concerns the compatibility of the New Economy with the Ghana Accelerated National Reserve Accumulation Policy (GANRAP), particularly its ambitious target of 15 months of import cover by 2028. The magnitude and feasibility of this target deserve scrutiny. According to the Bank of Ghana, gross international reserves declined from US$13.83 billion (5.7 months of import cover) in December 2025 to US$11.07 billion (4.2 months) in August 2026. At August’s implied monthly import-cover denominator, reaching 15 months would require reserves of roughly US$39.5 billion—about US$28.5 billion above the August stock within approximately two years. Meanwhile, scheduled external debt amortisation is projected to increase from GH¢24.8 billion in 2026 to GH¢35.5 billion in 2027, representing substantial foreign-exchange obligations that must be accommodated alongside the reserve accumulation strategy. These obligations coincide with the government’s intention to accelerate productive investment under the New Economy, which will likely increase imports of machinery, equipment and intermediate inputs before generating additional export earnings. Consequently, the government faces the challenge of simultaneously financing investment-related imports, meeting rising external debt obligations and accumulating international reserves at an unprecedented pace. The potential fiscal trade-off is equally important. In the 2026 Mid-Year Budget Review, the government allocated GH¢5 billion to GoldBod while reducing planned capital expenditure by an equivalent amount. Although acquiring reserve assets differs from ordinary expenditure, these adjustments raise questions about the opportunity costs of prioritising reserve accumulation over growth-enhancing investment. While stronger international reserves and productive investment can reinforce each other over time, the scale and timing of GANRAP’s targets raise legitimate questions about their compatibility with the New Economy. The 2027 Budget must therefore provide a convincing explanation of how the government intends to reconcile these competing demands without allowing the pursuit of an exceptionally ambitious reserve target to constrain productive investment and economic growth. Conclusion The New Economy represents an opportunity for Ghana to translate recent macroeconomic stability into sustained economic growth. However, its success will depend on whether the government channels the additional fiscal space into genuinely productive investment, finances the resulting deficit without undermining private-sector credit, and reconciles its growth ambitions with GANRAP’s aggressive reserve accumulation targets. The 2027 Budget must demonstrate that these policy objectives are mutually consistent and, ultimately, capable of delivering higher productivity, employment and household incomes.

items.title: Thirteen migrants die after boat sinks off Crete
items.description: At least 13 people have died after a boat carrying migrants sank off the coast of the Greek island of Crete. The coastguard said it had rescued 18 people, all of whom were Sudanese nationals. Four of the survivors were taken to hospital, including a toddler. Authorities said it was not immediately clear what caused the deaths, but they believe the boat had been at sea for days and had struggled to reach shore due to strong winds. Crete remains one of several key gateways for migrants attempting to reach Europe from the Middle East and North Africa, with more than 22,000 of the 86,400 sea arrivals so far this year landing in Crete alone. One unnamed coastguard official who spoke to news agency Reuters on condition of anonymity said the survivors were “shivering from the cold”. The migrants’ boat was spotted by a Moroccan-flagged container ship about 15 nautical miles (28km) off Crete’s coast. The Greek coastguard rescued another 187 people in three separate incidents off the coast of Greece on Monday. More than 37,000 migrants have arrived in Greece so far this year, UN figures show, already surpassing the number who arrived in the entirety of 2025. The Greek government has announced plans to deal with the influx, including opening a temporary housing complex near the Cretan capital, Heraklion. Greece was at the heart of Europe’s migration crisis in 2015-16, when nearly a million people arrived on its islands, mostly from Turkey. Arrivals later fell as border controls tightened, but crossings from Libya have surged in recent years, particularly among people fleeing conflict in Sudan and seeking better economic opportunities from countries including Bangladesh.

items.title: Court dismisses Maihaja’s suit against Wali’s APC ticket
items.description: By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman, Damaturu A Federal High Court sitting in Damaturu, Yobe State, has dismissed a suit challenging the emergence of Alhaji Baba Malam Wali as the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for the 2027 general election. The suit was instituted by Engr. Mustapha Yunusa Maihaja, an aspirant in the party’s May 21 governorship primary, who alleged irregularities and non-compliance with the APC’s electoral guidelines. In a judgment delivered on Monday, November 9, 2026, Justice Fatima Murtala Amin held that the suit was statute-barred, having been filed outside the legally prescribed timeframe. The court also found that Maihaja failed to establish his allegations, particularly the claim of over-voting during the governorship primary. Justice Amin upheld a preliminary objection challenging the competence of the suit, thereby dismissing the case on procedural grounds. On the substantive issues, the judge identified material contradictions and inconsistencies in the testimonies of the plaintiff’s witnesses, describing the evidence as unreliable and insufficient to support the allegations. The court further held that even if the suit had been filed within the prescribed timeframe, it would still have failed on its merits because the plaintiff did not provide credible evidence to establish the alleged over-voting. Wali emerged winner of the APC governorship primary with 236,711 votes, securing the party’s ticket for the 2027 governorship election in the state. Reacting to the judgment, Wali’s Press Secretary, Shuaibu Abdullahi, commended the court for its consideration of the issues raised in the suit. “We commend the Court for its painstaking consideration of the issues and reaffirm our confidence in the judiciary as the ultimate guardian of justice and the rule of law,” Abdullahi said. The judgment dismisses the legal challenge to Wali’s emergence as the APC governorship candidate, leaving his party ticket intact ahead of the 2027 general election. items.title: Offa robbery: Saraki faults Kwara govt over amended charges
items.description: Former Senate President, Bukola Saraki, has criticised the Kwara State Government over its decision to amend the criminal charges filed against him and former Governor Abdulfatah Ahmed in connection with the 2018 Offa bank robbery. Saraki described the development as an abuse of the judicial process, questioning the basis for the government’s decision to drop 18 of the original 20 counts and proceed with an amended four-count charge. In a statement issued on Monday by his media aide, Yusuph Olaniyonu, the former Senate President accused the administration of Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq of pursuing the case for political reasons. The Kwara State Government had, in an application filed on Monday before the state High Court in Ilorin, sought permission to proceed with an amended four-count charge against Saraki, Ahmed and two other defendants. The amended charge, dated November 6, 2026, retains two allegations bordering on conspiracy to belong to a gang of thieves and belonging to a gang of thieves. It also introduces two additional counts relating to the alleged concealment of a Lexus RX Jeep bearing the inscription ‘SARAKI’ as its plate number. Reacting, Saraki said the government had abandoned 18 charges relating to armed robbery after allegedly failing to establish a case against him and Ahmed. He said the government had, since April 2026, been pursuing their arraignment at the State High Court and the Court of Appeal without success. “Last weekend, the state government that has set its legal team to be shuttling between the State High Court and the Court of Appeal seeking without success since April 2026 to arraign the two predecessors of Mr Abdulrazaq on charges of armed robbery suddenly made a U-turn and dropped all 18 charges relating to armed robbery on the Offa case,” the statement said. Saraki alleged that the decision to amend the charges followed the government’s inability to substantiate the allegations against the two former governors. “For fear of failure, the government has chosen to change gear and explore yet other baseless charges,” he said. He described the amendment as evidence, in his view, that the allegations against him and Ahmed lacked a credible factual foundation. “The amendment to the charge sheet only reveals that there was no case against these gentlemen from the beginning and what the state government is indulging in is abuse of powers, a travesty of the justice system, and mockery of the prosecutorial powers of the state,” he added. The former Senate President also questioned the government’s decision to discontinue the 18 counts after allegedly spending close to N100 million publicising its claims against the defendants in national newspapers earlier in the year. He argued that the money could have been channelled into public projects rather than prosecuting allegations he described as unfounded. Saraki further alleged that the criminal proceedings were politically motivated, particularly because they were instituted in the build-up to the 2027 general elections. He also claimed that individuals allegedly connected to the state government had encouraged relatives of the robbery victims to institute a separate civil action against him and Ahmed. The former Senate President said his lawyers were prepared to challenge the amended charges in court, expressing confidence that the allegations would not succeed. He disclosed that the development coincided with his visit to Offa and other communities in Kwara South to campaign for Peoples Democratic Party candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. According to him, the reception he received during the visit indicated that residents had not accepted the allegations linking him to the robbery incident. Saraki also referred to alleged public statements by some former supporters of the governor, who reportedly claimed that the Offa robbery allegations were used to mobilise political support against him during the 2019 elections. The 2018 Offa robbery, which involved attacks on several banks and police facilities in Offa, Kwara State, resulted in the deaths of several people, including police officers and civilians. The amended charges are subject to determination by the court. The post Offa robbery: Saraki faults Kwara govt over amended charges appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Barcelona teenager Pau Cubarsí wins 2026 Golden Boy Award
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Barcelona centre-back Pau Cubarsí has won the 2026 Golden Boy award, becoming the first defender since Matthijs de Ligt in 2018 to receive the honour. The 19-year-old was recognised after a standout year with Barcelona and Spain. He helped Barça win a second consecutive LaLiga title and was part of Spain’s World Cup-winning team in North America, where he was named Young Player of the Tournament. “I’m very proud to receive the award, and I thank all the people who voted for me,” Cubarsí said in a video broadcast by Tuttosport at the ceremony. “It’s been a spectacular year, and we’re going for more,” he added. Cubarsí told Reuters that defenders can struggle to attract the same attention as attacking players. “It’s harder for defenders to get recognition… we’re less in the spotlight,” he said. “Perhaps our work isn’t as visible because, at the end of the day, the forwards score lots of goals, provide assists, play a more attractive style of football, are more eye-catching.” Spain conceded only one goal in eight matches en route to winning the World Cup, and Cubarsí played a key role in the team’s defence. He becomes the fourth Barcelona player to win the men’s award in the last six years, following teammates Pedri, Gavi and Lamine Yamal. Previous winners include Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappé and Erling Haaland. The Golden Boy award, established by Italian newspaper Tuttosport in 2003, recognises the best under-21 player in a top European division. Journalists vote from a shortlist of nominees. Real Madrid and Sweden forward Felicia Schroeder won the 2026 Golden Girl award. The post Barcelona teenager Pau Cubarsí wins 2026 Golden Boy Award appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tinubu: Wike promises N10m reward for FCT Councillors who deliver for APC
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has announced a financial incentive of N10 million for every councillor who successfully delivers their respective political ward for the All Progressives Congress APC and President Bola Tinubu in the upcoming general elections. Addressing stakeholders, traditional leaders, and political actors in Kwali, Wike explained that the initiative is part of a broad grassroots mobilisation strategy designed to rally maximum support at the grassroots level. “Any councillor that delivers his ward will get N10 million reward. Therefore, go and meet your leaders, go and meet your youth groups, go and consult with associations. Let’s deliver our ward to Mr President,” Wike urged the gathering. In addition to the electoral incentive, the FCT minister addressed structural and welfare concerns raised by local leaders, notably responding to an appeal by the Chairman of the National Councillors Forum of Nigeria (FCT Chapter), Gambo Hamza. Hamza had drawn attention to the disparity and low earnings of councillors in the territory – noting a monthly salary of N260,000 – which Wike termed unacceptable. The Minister promised to engage the permanent secretary and relevant administrative offices to review the remuneration structure, bypassing bureaucratic bottlenecks where possible to improve local governance welfare. Wike also underscored his administration’s dedication to gender inclusivity, emphasizing the need to increase women’s active participation in governance. Wike did not also mince words regarding what he described as the historical marginalisation of the FCT. He pointed out the stark disproportion in legislative distribution, questioning how a fast-growing population of six to seven million residents is restricted to only one Senate seat and a minimal number of House of Representatives seats. Comparing the FCT to other states with lesser populations boasting three senators and up to ten representatives, Wike maintained that structural fairness must be championed to give the nation’s capital adequate voice and equity. items.title: Chômage : Chahid veut une stratégie nationale consensuelle
items.description: Devant les députés, le ministre de l’Emploi et du Dialogue social a prévenu que le chômage ne se combattra plus à coups de slogans. Chiffres à l’appui, Abderrahim Chahid a défendu l’idée d’un cap national partagé et proposé de convoquer une troisième Conférence nationale sur l’emploi. Le ministre de l’Emploi et du Dialogue social, Abderrahim Chahid, a livré ce lundi 9 novembre 2026, lors de la séance hebdomadaire consacrée aux questions orales à la Chambre des représentants, un diagnostic sans fard du marché du travail. Son message tient en une phrase : le Maroc a besoin d’une stratégie nationale sur laquelle les forces du pays s’accordent, car la lutte contre le chômage ne peut plus reposer sur des mots d’ordre. Pour le ministre, le dossier de l’emploi dépasse largement le périmètre d’un seul département. Le gouvernement l’a certes inscrit parmi ses priorités, a-t-il rappelé, mais le sujet dépend avant tout de la capacité de l’économie à créer de la richesse, de l’orientation des investissements vers les secteurs productifs et de la qualité d’une formation en phase avec les besoins des entreprises. Les chiffres qu’il a présentés dessinent un tableau contrasté. Le taux de chômage s’est établi à 10,5 % au troisième trimestre 2026, contre 10,3 % à la même période de l’an dernier. Dans le même temps, l’emploi rémunéré a progressé de 158 000 postes nets sur un an. Le ministre a expliqué que le recul enregistré d’un trimestre à l’autre est lié, en partie, à des facteurs agricoles, ce qui rappelle le poids de la saisonnalité et de la pluviométrie dans l’équation de l’emploi. © Mounir Mehimdate Ce sont toutefois les catégories les plus fragiles qui concentrent l’essentiel des inquiétudes. Chez les 15-24 ans, le chômage atteint 30,5 %, un niveau qui fait de la jeunesse l’un des grands défis du moment. Abderrahim Chahid a également pointé les difficultés d’insertion des diplômés et le recul de la participation des femmes au marché du travail, tombée sous la barre des 18 %. Pour lui, ces deux phénomènes révèlent des déséquilibres plus profonds que le simple nombre d’emplois disponibles. Il en a tiré une conclusion de méthode : traiter ces déséquilibres suppose de regarder la nature même de la croissance économique, l’adéquation entre les cursus de formation et les besoins des entreprises, ainsi que les écarts entre territoires. Il a insisté sur la nécessité de faire évoluer les politiques publiques et d’en améliorer l’efficacité, plutôt que de se contenter de mesures conjoncturelles. Les ambitions affichées sont élevées. Selon le programme gouvernemental 2026-2031, l’exécutif vise la création d’environ un million d’emplois sur la législature, la réduction du taux de chômage à 7 % d’ici 2031 et la hausse du taux d’activité des femmes à 21,2 %. Le ministre a reconnu que ces objectifs exigent un consensus national et une approche fondée sur la construction d’une économie productive, capable de générer des emplois, adossée à un renforcement de l’État social qui produise des résultats tangibles. © Mounir Mehimdate C’est dans cette logique qu’Abderrahim Chahid a appelé à l’organisation d’une troisième conférence nationale sur l’emploi, après celles tenues à Marrakech en 1998 puis en 2005. L’objectif serait d’évaluer l’expérience passée et de mesurer si les institutions existantes sont en mesure d’accompagner les mutations du marché du travail comme les attentes des jeunes. Le ministre a aussi plaidé pour la réactivation des instances consultatives consacrées à l’emploi, en premier lieu le Conseil supérieur de promotion de l’emploi, ainsi que les conseils régionaux et provinciaux. Créés pour offrir des espaces de concertation, d’évaluation des politiques et de proposition de mesures, ces organes sont restés longtemps en sommeil, a-t-il regretté. Abderrahim Chahid a enfin relié cette orientation aux hautes directives royales appelant à valoriser les potentialités économiques des territoires et à encourager les initiatives et les investissements locaux, afin que le développement se traduise concrètement dans la vie des citoyens. L’emploi, a-t-il souligné, exige désormais une coordination entre l’ensemble des acteurs économiques, sociaux et institutionnels, dans le cadre d’une vision nationale qui dépasse les interventions sectorielles. The post Chômage : Chahid veut une stratégie nationale consensuelle appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Trafic de visas au Consulat d’Espagne à Alger : 120 millions DA investis dans l’immobilier
items.description: Du nouveau dans l’affaire de corruption et de trafic de visas au consulat d’Espagne à Alger. Les enquêteurs espagnols ont déterminé la destination d’une partie de l'argent ramassé par les mis en cause. Une somme importante a été investie dans l’immobilier à Alger. L'affaire a éclaté en avril 2026 lorsque Vicente Moreno, numéro deux du consulat d'Espagne à Alger, et Mohamed Boutouchent, un employé local, ont été arrêtés en Espagne et mis en examen. L'épouse de Moreno, Amina Nessrine Beljoudi, de nationalité algérienne, a aussi été mise en examen. Trafic de visas pour l'Espagne : 6 acquisitions immobilières à Alger En septembre dernier, une juge de l’Audience nationale à Madrid a inculpé Maua Belkacemi, secrétaire du consul, Hocine Malek et Lylia Dricy, employés administratifs chargés du traitement des visas. La société indienne TLS Contact, prestataire de la collecte et du traitement des demandes de visas, a été également inculpée. Les mis en cause sont soupçonnés d'avoir mis en place un système d’octroi illégal de visas moyennant de fortes sommes, jusqu'à 25.000 euros par famille. Les enquêteurs espagnols ont pu déterminer où est cachée au moins une partie du pactole ainsi ramassé sur plusieurs années. Selon le journal espagnol The Objective, l’unité de lutte contre la criminalité financière et économique (UDEF) de la police espagnole a mis au jour six propriétés immobilières à Alger liées au système de trafic. Le montant des acquisitions s'élève à 12 milliards de centimes Au cours des interrogatoires, les agents inculpés ont révélé aux juges que Moreno et son épouse posséderaient également des propriétés au Portugal. Le couple qui dirigeait le trafic a acquis au moins six propriétés à Alger sur une période de cinq ans, entre 2016 et 2021, ce qui suppose, écrit le média, que le trafic présumé de visas au sein du consulat espagnol remonte à au moins une décennie. Le montant total des acquisitions s'élève à 120 millions de dinars algériens, soit « environ 783.919 euros au taux de change actuel », ont précisé à la justice les agents inculpés. La moyenne de 20 millions de dinars (deux milliards de centimes) par bien immobilier correspond au niveau des prix appliqués à l'époque par les promoteurs immobiliers privés dans la capitale algérienne. Un trafic qui va au-delà des visas Schengen La police et la justice ont pris en charge l’affaire à la suite d’un signalement du ministère espagnol de l'Intérieur faisant état d’un trafic de visas au consulat d'Espagne à Alger. Les membres du réseau sont accusés de « traitement irrégulier des visas, des permis de séjour et des autorisations de travail dans le but de faciliter l'entrée de ressortissants algériens dans l'espace Schengen », alors que les bénéficiaires ne remplissaient pas les conditions requises pour l'obtention d'un visa. Outre l’octroi illégal de visa, le système incluait parfois l'obtention d’un statut de résident dans l’espace Schengen, en Espagne ou en France notamment, « par le biais de réseaux organisés qui prennent en charge la dernière étape » de ces opérations frauduleuses. L’article Trafic de visas au Consulat d’Espagne à Alger : 120 millions DA investis dans l’immobilier est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Access to Justice: Head of India’s Rights Body meets CJN, signs MoU with NHRC
items.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – A high-level delegation from India’s National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) met with the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN) on Monday to underscore the judiciary’s complementary role in enhancing access to justice. The delegation, led by a retired Supreme Court of India judge, Justice V. Ramasubramanian, was accompanied on the visit by the Executive Secretary of Nigeria’s NHRC, Dr. Tony Ojukwu, SAN, and top officials of the Commission. Although the meeting was held behind closed doors, Ojukwu, SAN, told journalists afterwards that the discussions centred on the need to guarantee speedy justice for victims of rights violations. Stressing the need for effective collaboration between human rights institutions in the country and the judiciary, the NHRC boss said the CJN had assured him of her commitment to the cause. He said the partnership with India is aimed at benefiting both countries through shared best practices, adding that it will further strengthen access to justice and human rights protection in Nigeria. According to him, the NHRC’s role is similar to that of the Indian commission. “Our visit here today is a recognition of the fact that human rights institutions need to work hand in hand with the judiciary to make sure that everybody is able to have access to justice and their rights respected. “We got the assurances today. The CJN reaffirmed the commitment of the judiciary to work with the human rights commission to make sure that both institutions work together for the benefit of the people of Nigeria. “This partnership will strengthen access to justice and the promotion and protection of human rights, and also ensure that such cases are given expedited action in court. “The role we play here is exactly the same role that the Indian commission plays, and the CJN also extolled the Indian judiciary for laying the foundation. “We practise in the area of public interest litigation, and we are able to share best practices in the work we do, both in India and Nigeria. “Through this memorandum of understanding, we are going to make sure that our people benefit from the good practices in India as well as those in Nigeria,” the NHRC Executive Secretary added. Likewise, Justice Ramasubramanian, who is the head of India’s NHRC, said his team’s visit to Nigeria was primarily for the signing of the MoU, which he said will benefit both countries. “We just had a meeting with the Honourable Chief Justice of Nigeria and her fellow justices of the Supreme Court of Nigeria. “It was a very fruitful meeting,” he added.
