items.title: Russell Brand jailed for 10 years for rape, assault
items.description: British comedian and TV star Russell Brand was Monday jailed for more than 10 years for a string of sex offences including rape, as the judge told him he had been a “sexual predator” whose fame had protected him. Brand, 51, showed no emotion as judge Joel Bennathan said he had acted with “staggering arrogance” and shown “contempt” for his victims, who had suffered significant and lasting harm. “About 20 years ago Russell Brand, you were becoming famous, you were clever, and in many people’s eyes you were funny and charismatic. You had also become a sexual predator,” he said. The judge said Brand’s status protected him until he was exposed in 2023 by journalists from the Sunday Times, The Times and the Channel 4 Dispatches programme, leading to women coming forward to make complaints to police. Bennathan paid tribute to the “determination and bravery” of the women, adding Brand had repeatedly acted “how you liked and when you liked, unhindered by the rules by which decent people live”. Brand’s wife Laura Gallacher, with whom he has three children, slumped in her seat in the public gallery of London’s Southwark Crown Court as the total sentence of 10 years and six months was announced. Brand told his wife, who has supported him in court throughout the case, “we’ll be OK”, before being led down to the cells. The disgraced star was convicted by a jury last week of one rape and three sexual assaults committed against four women between 2004 and 2009. Brand, who has reinvented himself as an online Christian guru, held a string of prayer beads and made the sign of the cross before one of his victims personally read out her impact statement from behind a screen. She said she had been left “traumatised” by the assault in a London bar in 2004. “For many years as his star was rising it was impossible to escape seeing him all over the media, being celebrated for his disgusting behaviour against women like it was all a joke,” she told the court. ‘Celebrated’ A second woman, a 21-year-old fan he raped in 2009 after they met at one of his shows, told the court she had felt she simply would “not be believed” if she reported him. “His fame, wealth and influence created a power imbalance which made me feel powerless,” she said. The hearing came as Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged to be “relentless in making whatever improvements we can” to provide more support for victims. Brand was cleared of two other alleged rapes and one count of attempted indecent assault. But he is facing further investigations after London police revealed rape allegations by two more women. From Channel 4 to MTV and an eponymous primetime show on BBC Radio 2, the wild-haired comedian’s obsession with sex and his no-holds barred delivery contributed to his notoriety. Brand denied the charges, but he admitted to being “extremely promiscuous” and using his fame to “facilitate sexual access”. ‘Wake-up call’ Born to working-class parents in Essex, east of London, in 1975, Brand dropped out of drama school before joining MTV at the age of 25. He had his own radio show at the BBC, which last week apologised for the “culture and failings” when Brand worked there between 2006 and 2008. Brand left the BBC after leaving a well-known actor sexually explicit messages on his answering machine about having slept with his granddaughter. He made a foray into Hollywood after a brief marriage in 2010 to US pop star Katy Perry. The court found him guilty of sexual assaults against an MTV worker, a Channel 4 worker and a Capital Radio employee, as well as raping a fan. The organisations that propped up Brand for years are now facing questions about how he continued for so long. British culture minister Lisa Nandy said men in power were still exploiting women in the media industry, saying his case was a “wake-up call”. Speaking outside court, the lead detective in the case Andy Furphy said the sentence was a “milestone” that had seen Brand finally “held accountable for his crimes”. And he praised the “immense bravery, dignity and resilience” of the victims who had had “to revisit deeply traumatic experiences”. As he left court, Brand’s father Ron Brand told reporters his son had been a “victim” and that both Russell and his daughter-in-law would be alright. “Yeah, he’s strong, he’s strong,” he said, when asked how his son would cope in jail, adding “she’s strong as well”, referring to Laura. items.title: UN Report Highlights North Korea’s Deepening Repression
items.description: Click to expand Image Soldiers participate in a commemorative march in Pyongyang, North Korea, on April 25, 2025, to mark the 93rd anniversary of the Korean People's Revolutionary Army. © 2025 KIM WON JIN/AFP via Getty Images United Nations Special Rapporteur Elizabeth Salmón addressed a UN General Assembly committee on October 27 following reports that North Korean authorities had increased the use of public executions, including for recent offenses. In her report, Salmón characterized the government’s use of the death penalty as “a criminal sanction [and] means of social, political and ideological control,” alongside expanded surveillance and tightened restrictions on basic freedoms. The report corroborates Human Rights Watch research documenting heightened ideological control since the start of Covid-19 and a recent Transitional Justice Working Group report that found death sentences in North Korea increased sharply since 2020, particularly for those accused of distributing foreign media in the country. As the United States and South Korea pursue diplomatic dialogues with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, the focus on security issues should not again displace North Korea’s many rights issues. UN human rights offices and independent experts have continued to monitor North Korea’s deteriorating rights situation despite difficult circumstances. However, UN member countries have not acted on this reporting and focused entirely on North Korea’s threats to international peace and security. But the threats North Korea poses are facilitated and directly linked to the country’s rights violations. As Salmón said, governments need to “[integrate] human rights considerations into all future engagement with [North Korea].” Multiple UN findings, statements by the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights, and UN Human Rights Council resolutions have affirmed that rights violations—forced labor, in particular—have enabled and remain linked to North Korea’s nuclear weapons program. The government devotes massive resources to maintaining its nuclear weapons and missile stockpiles while many North Koreans face chronic hunger. Security and rights issues need to be addressed together. The UN General Assembly has the power to forge these connections, even as the Security Council remains deadlocked. The General Assembly should request additional reporting on these issues from other UN bodies or explore independent investigations into connections between rights abuses and other issues and North Korea’s threats to security. And before any diplomatic talks commence, it should recommend that all dialogues with North Korea address rights and security concerns in tandem.

items.title: How Ugly Metro Sweaters Became Chic
items.description: The nation’s transit systems have an unlikely side hustle. The Los Angeles Metro is selling T-shirts that label its riders a Bus Baddie and a Metro Mamí and encourage locals to Ride the D (a suggestive reference to a recent line extension). The NYC Ferry offers hats and shirts that read The People’s Yacht . In Washington, D.C., locals have started wearing the Metro system’s merch like it’s their alma mater. A recent pop-up shop drew some 10,000 visitors with so many offerings that a patron could emerge decked out from head to toe in Metro. “It was mobbed,” Emily Wasek, a think-tank staffer and self-described devotee of D.C.’s Yellow Line, told me. “People were running against traffic in the street to cut in front of people.” The appetite for transit wear appears to be huge (or at least hugely noticeable on social media). When Amtrak announced a new, limited-edition T-shirt last week featuring trains in the style of superheroes on a movie poster, commenters praised the national rail system for “giving the people what they want.” Then they demanded more. At their best, transit systems can weave a city’s culture together. As basic public services, however, they are not typically fodder for fashion. But then again, people aren’t ordinarily so isolated from one another, the cost of living isn’t normally this high, and subway systems aren’t usually this savvy at marketing. From talking with transit-wear enthusiasts, I got the sense that a mix of economic and social circumstances has sparked their desire to elevate public transit, an anti-status symbol of sorts, to the front of their clothes. The fact that transit branding tends to have sleek designs and a retro look certainly helps. Consumers have long made themselves billboards for various brands that don’t necessarily need their help, be it Nike or Costco, and a more cynical take might be that today’s transitphilia really just shows that anything can be commodified. At the same time, people are not lining up around the block for ride-sharing T-shirts or rental-car Christmas sweaters. Something more substantial is happening here, even if some of the hype might be closer to virtue signalling with an urban-planning bent. Public-transit fans and marketing and design professors I spoke with repeatedly likened transit merch to sports-team apparel: a way for people to signal their ties to a community. With so much talk about affordability and loneliness, a public amenity that physically binds a city together may be the perfect mascot for 21st-century urban life. When people are cheering for a metro system, they’re cheering for connection—even if that connection comes in the form of strangers bumping into one another on rattling cars, 100-something feet beneath the earth. [ Read: Do yourself a favor and go find a ‘third place’ ] This may sound like a lot to put on a mere transit system, but conversations about public transportation have a way of getting deep. Samuel Littauer, a 28-year-old in D.C., told me that he sees the subway system as the “great unifier.” At the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority sale, Littauer bought one T-shirt highlighting the system’s modernist architecture and another that shows a vintage Metro bus. He said he hopes that wearing them will allow him to connect with people who love the region like he does. Georgetta Nicol, the director of marketing at WMATA, suggested that the rush for Metro products is linked to a post-pandemic craving to be around others. She (and others I spoke with) were even willing to stretch the definition of third place —which describes spaces outside of home and work where people socialize and build community—to include public transit. One of WMATA’s hats is a bid for social interaction: Ask me about Metro . Illustration by The Atlantic. Sources: Bay Area Rapid Transit; DC Metro Store; Official Los Angeles Metro Shop. For some, an affection for public transit is already a lifestyle of sorts. Wasek hosts a “Metro Gala” each year, where friends dress up as interpretations of Metro stops. The winners for best dressed receive Metro merch. Jerome Horne, who works at the Maryland Transit Administration, owns nearly a dozen public-transit Christmas sweaters (and counting) and maintains a wider collection of transit items that he calls the “International Micro Museum of Transit.” He sees the broad affinity for public transit as part of a resurgence in esteem for public institutions. Transit is also “one of the last places you could go if you’re anyone and just exist,” he told me. Such appreciation may also be born of changes to how Americans get around: Fewer young people want to drive , cars are expensive, and there may be no more consequential political issue right now than the price of gas. There’s a way in which the rise of transit chic could parallel how recessions can make vintage clothes popular. People are making what they can have trendy. Still, “I think there was always a ‘cool’ there, even if not everyone recognized it,” Horne said. Public transit occupies a strange, contradictory place in the American psyche. In cities where cars reign, it can be heavily stigmatized. In a few major urban centers, though, it has a kind of cultural cachet. Images of the New York subway are as ingrained in the city’s identity as the Statue of Liberty. The NYC subway map decorates dorm rooms and apartments. Massimo Vignelli’s 1972 redesign, which smoothed the map into a minimalist artwork of straightforward lines and simple labels, is even included in the Museum of Modern Art’s collection, cementing it in design history. The license that Lynne Lambert obtained in the ’90s to produce merchandise with the Metropolitan Transportation Authority’s recognizable colored circles and other logos made the aesthetic into a business (one that’s still running today). This most recent wave of transit-clothes hype might be traced back to 2021, when Bay Area Rapid Transit, in the San Francisco Bay Area, offered 150 ugly Christmas sweaters for sale online. They were gone in 40 minutes. Eventually, the endeavor earned the transportation authority more than $100,000 in one season. Every year since, BART has offered the signature holiday product and has been joined by a growing number of transit lines in Philadelphia, Toronto, Milwaukee, Chicago, Portland, and more. “It’s now almost become a competition between agencies,” Horne, the sweater connoisseur, said. Success doesn’t always require tapping the holiday spirit. Many of the items at the D.C. Metro’s recent pop-up were hyperlocal—station-specific hats or quarter-zips color-coded by subway line. Often, systems adapt wayfinding features, such as signs and arrows, into clothing patterns. In Atlanta, the Metropolitan Atlanta Rapid Transit Authority sells “pylon” winter hats that match the blue-yellow-and-orange color scheme used within the system. Illustration by The Atlantic. Sources: Chicago Transit Authority Shop; DC Metro Store; ItsMARTAMerch; NYC Ferry. Marc Choi, a graphic-design professor at the George Washington University, told me that although wayfinding signs are supposed to be functional and “there but not there,” people build a subconscious relationship with them. In this way, a system’s design features become almost as recognizable as a city’s skyline, but they’re also more personal: They’re the city’s visual language. If you take transit, you’re fluent in it. “People have a very strong relationship with their day-to-day commute,” Choi said. “I think pop-up shops and this merch is just a fun way to channel that.” Sometimes, the offerings go heavy on the fun: Metro sells swimsuits that read Foggy Bottom across the butt. (It’s the name of a station.) A little personality can give some verve to well-worn systems. But no one is going to buy transit merch if they don’t first enjoy using the system. I was surprised, for instance, to stumble upon a cheerful Christmas sweater for a regional train line that I can describe only as my locomotive nemesis (no thank you). But when the strategy works, it really works. I’ve been given a T-shirt that features a photo of the D.C. Metro’s brutalist “waffle” ceilings not once, but twice. I kept even the second one because I didn’t know how to say I already had it—and because they are both, to use the shirts’ coinage, brutiful .

items.title: Libéralisme à l’européenne : en France, le prix du gaz va augmenter pour le quatrième mois d’affilée
items.description: La facture de chauffage va s'alourdir cet hiver pour les quelque six millions de Francais ayant souscrit une offre indexee sur le prix moyen du gaz. Ce 9 novembre, alors qu'une hausse de 6,6 % de ce meme prix de reference vient tout juste d'entrer en vigueur, la Commission de regulation de l'energie (CRE) a annonce une nouvelle hausse de 5,8 % a compter du 1er decembre. Ces augmentations s'ajoutent a celles de 6,3 % en octobre et de 5,6 % en septembre. Il s'agit de la « consequence d'une augmentation des prix sur les marches du gaz au mois d'octobre comparativement a septembre », s'est defendue la CRE. « On subit un prix de marche international, on importe 95 % de notre gaz », a declare a l'AFP la presidente de la CRE, Emmanuelle Wargon. « Ce prix reflete le fait qu'il y a moins d'offre depuis la crise dans le detroit d'Ormuz », a ajoute cette ancienne ministre macroniste du Logement (2020-2022), alors que l'UE s'entete a fermer le robinet du gaz russe. Gaz : la facture des Francais « explose » « La facture annuelle 2026 pour un consommateur moyen augmentera de 11,8 % par rapport a la facture annuelle 2025 (soit +143 euros TTC) », a egalement indique la CRE. Un chiffre fortement eloigne de celui avance par le site Hellowatt, selon lequel la facture moyenne annuelle des Francais atteindrait 565 euros « en a peine dix mois », entre janvier et octobre 2026, face a un prix du gaz qui « explose ». Ce prix dit « de repere » remplace depuis l'ete 2023, au nom de l'ouverture du marche de l'energie a la concurrence promue par Bruxelles, le tarif reglemente de vente du gaz (TRVG) et sert de reference aux fournisseurs d'energie pour etablir leurs tarifs. Le TRVG, juge « contraire au droit europeen » par le Conseil d'etat en juillet 2017, etait en vigueur en France depuis les annees d'apres-guerre et ambitionnait de permettre a tous les Francais d'acceder au gaz naturel grâce a un prix encadre par les pouvoirs publics.

items.title: FRMF : l’Assemblée générale élective fixée au 12 décembre
items.description: La Fédération Royale Marocaine de Football (FRMF) a fixé au samedi 12 décembre 2026 la date de sa prochaine Assemblée générale élective. La date limite pour le dépôt des candidatures a, quant à elle, été arrêtée au vendredi 4 décembre. Réuni ce lundi 9 novembre au siège de la FRMF sous la présidence de Fouzi Lekjaa, le Comité directeur de la Fédération Royale Marocaine de Football a arrêté le calendrier de la prochaine Assemblée générale élective. Selon le communiqué publié à l’issue de la réunion, l’Assemblée générale élective se tiendra le samedi 12 décembre 2026 à partir de 16h00. Les candidats devront déposer leur dossier au plus tard le vendredi 4 décembre 2026, conformément aux règlements en vigueur. Cette échéance intervient alors que la FRMF poursuit ses travaux sur plusieurs dossiers liés au développement du football national. Le Comité directeur a notamment examiné la situation des championnats professionnels, amateurs et féminins, ainsi que les préparatifs liés aux prochaines échéances sportives. Lors de cette réunion, Fouzi Lekjaa a insisté sur la nécessité de respecter les dispositions légales et réglementaires encadrant la prochaine Assemblée générale élective. Le président de la FRMF a également appelé les clubs à tourner la page des litiges et des conflits, en mettant l’accent sur le respect des règlements, la bonne gouvernance et la transparence dans la gestion des compétitions nationales. La réunion a par ailleurs permis de faire le point sur plusieurs chantiers du football marocain, notamment la programmation du championnat et de la Coupe du Trône, le développement du football amateur et féminin ainsi que la formation des arbitres et des cadres techniques. Le football féminin parmi les priorités Concernant le football féminin, la FRMF prévoit notamment de renforcer la visibilité du championnat national. Fouzi Lekjaa a appelé à une couverture télévisuelle accrue, avec deux rencontres diffusées chaque semaine, afin d’améliorer l’exposition des compétitions féminines. La Fédération a également annoncé l’acquisition de 24 grands autocars destinés aux clubs des première et deuxième divisions nationales, dans le cadre du programme FIFA-Forward. Une augmentation des primes financières accordées aux clubs champions est également envisagée. La prochaine échéance est désormais fixée : les candidatures devront être déposées avant le 4 décembre, avant la tenue de l’Assemblée générale élective le 12 décembre 2026. The post FRMF : l’Assemblée générale élective fixée au 12 décembre appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: CAN 2027, Algérie – Togo : les Fennecs perdent deux joueurs clés
items.description: Coup dur pour l’équipe d’Algérie à une semaine du match contre le Togo dans le cadre de la 3e journée des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027, prévu le 14 novembre au stade Hocine Aït Ahmed de Tizi-Ouzou. Après le départ du gardien Abdellatif Ramdane, qui a été libéré par le sélectionneur national Brahim Hemdani à la suite du décès de son père hier dimanche, les Fennecs ont reçu une autre mauvaise nouvelle ce lundi. L’attaquant de Hull City, Mohamed Bachir Belloumi, et le défenseur de Brighton, Jaouen Hadjam sont déclarés forfaits pour blessure. Face au Togo le 14 novembre à Tizi-Ouzou et le 17 novembre à Lomé, l’équipe nationale sera privée de ces deux éléments clés, titulaires depuis l’arrivée de Hemdani à la tête des Fennecs en septembre dernier. Équipe d’Algérie : Hemdani fait appel à Fahem Benaïssa pour remplacer Jaouen Hadjam « Souffrant de blessures, l’attaquant Bachir Belloumi et le défenseur Jaouen Hadjam sont forfaits pour la double confrontation face au Togo, comptant pour les éliminatoires de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations 2027 », a indiqué la Fédération algérienne de football. Pour remplacer Hadjam, Brahim Hemdani a fait appel au défenseur Fahem Benaïssa-Yahia, qui rejoindra le Centre technique national (CTN) de Sidi Moussa en début de soirée. Benaïssa, 24 ans, est un défenseur qui peut évoluer à gauche ou à droite. Il évolue au club italien de Mantova 1911 (Série B). C’est sa première convocation en équipe nationale. Peu avant cette annonce, Brahim Hemdani a convoqué le gardien de l’Olympique Akbou Rayane Yeseli pour remplacer le portier du MCA Abdellatif Ramdane. Pour Bachir Belloumi, aucun remplaçant n’a été appelé. L’article CAN 2027, Algérie – Togo : les Fennecs perdent deux joueurs clés est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Ambassador Smith calls for compulsory military training to engage Ghana’s youth
items.description: Ghana’s Ambassador to the United States, Victor Smith, has proposed compulsory military training for young people as part of efforts to promote discipline and address what he describes as growing indiscipline in the country. Speaking in an interview on JoyNews, Mr Smith suggested that young people leaving school should undergo military training for up to two years to instil discipline and keep them productively engaged. “Why don’t we let the young people who come out of school do two years or so in military training? Just to sort of, if you like, put some discipline in people,” he said. The Ambassador argued that keeping young people engaged in structured activities could help address idleness, which he associated with corruption and other social problems. “The devil finds work for idle hands. So we put them in the military training; they’re not idle anymore,” he said. He suggested that participants could be deployed to agricultural activities, including mass production, as part of the proposed programme. Mr Smith also proposed reviving the Workers’ Brigade model, under which young people would be engaged in agriculture and paid for their work. “I want you to think about another step—what used to exist in the Workers’ Brigade, where they will go into agriculture, mass production, they will get paid for the food that we are producing and selling to regional markets or abroad and pay them,” he said. He argued that the initiative could combine skills training with productive employment, while supporting food production and creating opportunities for young people. Under his proposal, the military training component would be government-supported, with participants trained and engaged in assigned activities rather than left without structured opportunities. Mr Smith said participation in the proposed programme should be compulsory and suggested that it could be linked to the National Service Authority. “It must be compulsory. Let’s say one year,” he said, adding that opportunities created through the Workers’ Brigade could provide a pathway into employment after the training period. He said a structured programme was necessary to ensure young people had meaningful activities and were not left to determine how to occupy their time without support. Ghana already operates a mandatory national service programme for eligible tertiary education graduates through the National Service Authority. Mr Smith’s proposal would go beyond the existing arrangement by introducing compulsory military training and potentially extending structured national service to young people leaving school.

items.title: Aéroport AST de Conakry : la SOGEAC lance la première Semaine de l’hospitalité pour faire du passager une priorité
items.description: La Société de gestion et d’exploitation des aéroports de Guinée (SOGEAC) a procédé, ce lundi 9 novembre 2026, au lancement officiel de la première édition de la « Semaine de l’hospitalité », placée sous le thème « L’humain au cœur de l’expérience client ». La cérémonie s’est déroulée dans l’enceinte du siège de la société, en présence de représentants du ministère des Transports, des compagnies aériennes et de plusieurs partenaires de la plateforme aéroportuaire. Prévue du 9 au 15 novembre 2026 à l’Aéroport international Ahmed-Sékou-Touré de Conakry, cette initiative s’inscrit dans la dynamique mondiale de la Customer Service Week. À travers cet événement, la SOGEAC entend renforcer la qualité de l’accueil, améliorer l’expérience des voyageurs et faire de la principale porte d’entrée aérienne de la Guinée une plateforme moderne, chaleureuse et conforme aux standards internationaux. Représentant la direction générale de la SOGEAC, le directeur général adjoint, Sékou Ahmed Tidjane Yansané, a souligné le caractère inédit de cette initiative dans l’histoire de l’aéroport, tout en rappelant l’importance stratégique de l’accueil dans l'image d'un pays. « Un aéroport n'est pas seulement une infrastructure de transport ; il est une porte d'entrée au pays, une vitrine de son identité et, pour chaque voyageur, souvent le premier et le dernier souvenir de son séjour », a-t-il déclaré. Pour lui, chaque interaction avec un passager contribue à façonner la perception de la Guinée à l'étranger. « Un sourire, une information fiable, une assistance attentive ou une prise en charge efficace contribuent directement à l'image de la Guinée. C'est cette conviction qui guide notre initiative », a-t-il expliqué. Il a ensuite décliné les quatre principaux objectifs de cette semaine : témoigner de la reconnaissance aux passagers à travers un accueil renforcé et des attentions particulières ; valoriser les femmes et les hommes qui travaillent quotidiennement sur la plateforme aéroportuaire ; renforcer l'écoute des voyageurs grâce aux enquêtes de satisfaction et aux échanges de proximité ; et promouvoir l'image de la Guinée à travers une expérience conforme à la réputation d'hospitalité du peuple guinéen. Il a notamment insisté sur la nécessité de reconnaître le travail des agents d'accueil, du personnel de sûreté et d'escale, des techniciens, des équipes de maintenance et de nettoyage, ainsi que des commerçants et des autres entreprises présentes sur la plateforme. Cette démarche intervient dans un contexte marqué par les ambitions de développement du pays, notamment à travers le programme Simandou 2040. Selon lui (Sékou Ahmed Tidjane Yansané), l'évolution des attentes des voyageurs et les exigences croissantes du transport aérien imposent une meilleure coordination entre les différents intervenants de l'aéroport. Dans cette perspective, il a annoncé la mise en place d'un comité de facilitation regroupant les acteurs intervenant aux différentes étapes du parcours des passagers. Sa mission consistera notamment à simplifier les procédures, fluidifier les déplacements, réduire les temps d'attente et améliorer durablement la qualité des services. « Aucun acteur ne peut agir seul. La performance d'un aéroport repose sur la coordination de tous », a-t-il fait remarquer, en évoquant le rôle de l'autorité de l'aviation civile, des services de défense et de sécurité, des services de contrôle aux frontières, des compagnies aériennes et des autres entreprises opérant sur la plateforme. Durant les sept jours de célébration, plusieurs activités sont annoncées, notamment un accueil renforcé des passagers, des animations culturelles, l'immersion des cadres dans les opérations de terrain, des cadeaux aux enfants, la promotion des produits locaux guinéens, des enquêtes de satisfaction et la distinction des collaborateurs les plus engagés. Il salué l'accompagnement des partenaires Servair, du salon Nimba et d'Easy Pom, avant de rendre hommage au président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, et au ministre des Transports pour leur soutien à la modernisation du secteur aéroportuaire. Prenant la parole au nom de l'Association des compagnies aériennes basées en Guinée, Kadiatou Bah a, pour sa part, salué cette initiative et félicité la direction générale de la SOGEAC pour son engagement en faveur de l'amélioration continue des services. « Nous souhaitons encourager et féliciter l'ensemble de la direction de la SOGEAC pour cette dynamique positive et ces initiatives qui contribuent à l'amélioration continue de la qualité des services et de l'expérience de nos clients communs », a-t-elle déclaré. Elle a réaffirmé leur disponibilité à accompagner cette dynamique de collaboration entre les différents acteurs du secteur aérien, dans l'intérêt des passagers. Représentant le ministre des Transports, la cheffe de cabinet du département, Fatoumata Bangoura, a également félicité le président du conseil d'administration, la direction générale et l'ensemble des équipes de la SOGEAC pour le lancement de cette première édition. Elle a estimé que cette initiative traduit une volonté de placer l'usager au centre des préoccupations et de faire de la qualité du service une priorité durable de la gouvernance aéroportuaire. « L'aéroport international Ahmed Sékou Touré est bien plus qu'une infrastructure de transport : il est la principale porte d'entrée aérienne de la République de Guinée. Il est la première image de notre pays pour celle qui arrive et la dernière pour celle qui repart », a-t-elle souligné. Pour la représentante du ministère, l'expérience d'un voyageur ne se limite pas aux conditions de son vol. Elle se construit également à travers la qualité de l'accueil, la clarté des informations fournies, la courtoisie des contrôles et la bonne prise en charge des bagages. Elle a ainsi rappelé que l'hospitalité constitue une valeur profondément ancrée dans la culture guinéenne, dont l'enjeu est désormais de faire un véritable standard professionnel, constant et partagé par tous les acteurs de la plateforme aéroportuaire. Elle a par ailleurs inscrit cette initiative dans la vision de modernisation portée par le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, notamment à travers le programme Simandou 2040. Selon elle, cette ambition de transformation économique ne se limite pas aux secteurs minier et industriel, mais concerne également les infrastructures de transport et la connectivité internationale. Dans cette dynamique, les plateformes aéroportuaires guinéennes sont appelées à répondre aux exigences internationales afin d'accueillir dans de meilleures conditions les investisseurs, les experts et les visiteurs attirés par les perspectives économiques du pays. Au nom du ministre des Transports, elle a enfin réaffirmé l'engagement du département à accompagner toutes les initiatives visant à améliorer la performance des plateformes aéroportuaires, à renforcer la sûreté et la sécurité de l'aviation civile, à moderniser les infrastructures et à promouvoir une véritable culture de la qualité conforme aux standards internationaux. Au-delà des festivités et des activités prévues, cette première Semaine de l'hospitalité ambitionne ainsi d'installer une nouvelle culture de service au sein de l'aéroport de Conakry. Comme l'a rappelé le représentant de la direction générale de la SOGEAC, l'hospitalité ne doit pas être un événement ponctuel, mais « un réflexe, un état d'esprit, une exigence et une culture partagée » au quotidien. Un pari qui vise à renforcer la confiance des voyageurs, la compétitivité de la plateforme aéroportuaire et, au-delà, l'attractivité de la Guinée. items.title: 2027: Stop following Tinubu to rallies, return to grassroots, Kalu tells APC leaders
items.description: Senator Orji Uzor Kalu has urged leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to stop following President Bola Tinubu from one campaign rally to another and concentrate on grassroots mobilisation in their respective states, local government areas and wards ahead of the 2027 general elections. Kalu, who represents Abia North Senatorial District and serves as Coordinator of Parliamentary Mobilisation for the South-East, made the call in a statement titled, “The APC Presidential Campaign Council and the Need for a Leaner Campaign Train.” He argued that Tinubu should be accompanied by a smaller campaign team, while other party leaders should remain in their respective political bases to engage voters and strengthen the party’s grassroots structures. The senator’s position comes days after the APC Presidential Campaign Council issued guidelines restricting ministers, political appointees and campaign council members to rallies organised in their respective home states. The circular, signed by the Director-General of the council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, on November 3, was addressed to directors and heads of directorates. It directed political appointees and other campaign officials to attend only rallies in their home states as part of efforts to improve coordination and grassroots mobilisation. The council also adopted what it described as the pyramid concept of mobilisation, which prioritises engagement at polling unit, ward, local government and state levels. Under the arrangement, campaign officials and party leaders are expected to concentrate on building support at the grassroots rather than concentrating around the President during rallies. Kalu cited his political activities in Abia State as an example of the importance of grassroots mobilisation. He recalled leading more than 4,000 APC members in his Igbere Ward A, Bende Local Government Area, during the party’s presidential primary in May. He said the exercise demonstrated the importance of building political support from the ward level. At the exercise, the returning officer, Mr Ulu Onwuchekwa, announced that Tinubu scored 4,986 votes in the ward. Tinubu had also urged members of the campaign council to take responsibility for mobilisation across the country, saying he would concentrate on governance. The President made the appeal on October 14 during the inauguration of the Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja. The campaign was subsequently flagged off in Kaduna on October 24, with plans to take the campaign to all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. Tinubu is, however, expected to personally attend rallies in only 12 states. The November 3 circular further directed campaign directorates without specific responsibilities at rallies to concentrate on their approved work plans and budgets. It also outlined the responsibilities of members of the APC National Working Committee, directing those outside designated national officers to focus on party administration and mobilisation in their respective states and geopolitical zones. The designated officers exempted from the restriction include the National Chairman, National Secretary, National Women Leader, National Youth Leader and National Organising Secretary. The guidelines are also intended to create opportunities for APC candidates contesting legislative positions to participate more actively in campaign activities in their respective states and constituencies. Kalu maintained that effective grassroots engagement would be critical to the party’s electoral prospects in 2027, stressing the need for leaders to maintain contact with voters and strengthen party structures at the ward level. He said the focus should be on direct engagement with constituents rather than the size of the entourage accompanying the President at campaign events. Kalu, a former governor of Abia State and former Senate Chief Whip, has remained active in APC political mobilisation in the South-East. The senator’s call reinforces the campaign council’s position that effective mobilisation requires party leaders to work within their designated areas and strengthen support from the grassroots ahead of the 2027 elections. items.title: Se faisant passer pour un Commandant de l’armée, il aurait escroqué plus de 100 millions GNF et 25 000 dollars
items.description: Un homme soupçonné d’avoir usurpé l’identité d’un haut responsable militaire guinéen pour extorquer d’importantes sommes d’argent à des personnalités et opérateurs économiques a été interpellé le vendredi 6 novembre 2026 à Conakry. Le mis en cause, Abdoulaye Mbalou Kaba, aurait ainsi engrangé plus de 100 millions de francs guinéens et 25 000 dollars américains grâce à de faux profils sur les réseaux sociaux, selon une information publiée ce lundi 9 novembre par Actuguinée.org. L’affaire met en lumière une présumée opération d’escroquerie reposant sur l’usurpation de l’identité du commandant Moriba Dentili Keïta, plus connu sous le surnom de «Commandant Kilo». Présenté à la presse ce lundi par la Direction centrale de lutte contre le crime organisé, Abdoulaye Mbalou Kaba est soupçonné d’avoir exploité l’image et le nom de cet officier pour tromper ses victimes. Selon les éléments de l’enquête, le suspect aurait mis en place, depuis 2023, un dispositif de fraude à travers de faux comptes sur WhatsApp, Signal et Facebook. Se faisant passer pour le haut responsable militaire, il aurait multiplié les demandes d’assistance financière auprès de plusieurs personnalités et opérateurs économiques. Parmi les victimes présumées figure Kaman Sadji, directeur général de FAP Gaz. Selon les informations communiquées par les enquêteurs et les déclarations du mis en cause, ce dernier lui aurait soutiré 75 millions de francs guinéens, 25 000 dollars américains, ainsi qu'une somme supplémentaire de 20 millions de francs guinéens par le biais d'Orange Money. Les fonds ainsi obtenus auraient notamment servi à financer son mariage, à louer et à meubler son domicile. Une autre partie, estimée à 35 millions de francs guinéens, aurait été remise à son grand frère pour la construction d’une maison au village. Face aux enquêteurs, Abdoulaye Mbalou Kaba aurait reconnu les faits et exprimé des regrets. Il soutient cependant avoir agi seul, affirmant ne pas entretenir de relations personnelles avec le commandant Moriba Dentili Keïta, dont il aurait frauduleusement utilisé l’identité. Une vigilance accrue face aux arnaques numériques À la suite de cette affaire, les services spéciaux appellent les citoyens à la prudence face aux sollicitations financières émanant de personnes prétendant être des proches ou des collaborateurs du «Commandant Kilo» ou d’autres officiers militaires. Ils recommandent de ne donner aucune suite à de telles demandes sans en avoir préalablement vérifié l’authenticité. Abdoulaye Mbalou Kaba doit être déféré devant le parquet pour répondre des faits présumés d’escroquerie, d’usurpation de titres, de faux et usage de faux et de cybercriminalité. L’enquête judiciaire devra désormais établir les responsabilités dans cette affaire. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Se faisant passer pour un Commandant de l’armée, il aurait escroqué plus de 100 millions GNF et 25 000 dollars est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: El Supremo rechaza suspender también el voto de los hijos de los nacionalizados por la ‘ley de nietos’
items.description: Los hijos de los españoles nacionalizados por la ley de nietos que vivan en el extranjero podrán votar el 29-N. El Tribunal Supremo ha renunciado a extender a este grupo la suspensión del derecho al sufragio que decretó en septiembre para los hijos y nietos de la emigración y el exilio que han obtenido la nacionalidad con la Ley de Memoria Democrática. Los magistrados han rechazado la petición de Iustitia Europa y de Vox, que reclamaron que la medida adoptada por los jueces para más de 163.000 nacionalizados como descendientes del exilio se extendiera a su vez a los hijos de estos, nacionalizados por otro apartado de la Ley de Memoria que no está afectado por la suspensión del voto acordada por el Supremo. La Abogacía del Estado se había opuesto a esa posibilidad y alegó que ampliar la suspensión del derecho al voto pondría en riesgo el cumplimiento de los trámites legales para el 29-N e incluso podría afectar al escrutinio. El tribunal coincide en que es demasiado “breve” el “lapso temporal” que queda hasta los comicios, por lo que opta por no ampliar la suspensión del voto. No obstante, en otra resolución notificada este martes, los jueces insisten en que los últimos datos aportados por el Gobierno acrecientan “los indicios racionales de presuntas irregularidades de gran relevancia en la configuración” del censo de españoles en el extranjero. items.title: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
items.description: France has accused Iran of being behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers. Speaking at a news conference, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the attack was carried out by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of Iran. He said the attack was “unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression”, adding that the country would “implement sanctions at the European level against all those responsible for this attack.” The cyber-attack last month saw fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across France heated up, which spoilt fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros. Then last week, dozens of supermarkets across seven other European countries were also impacted by a cyber-attack that targeted fridges and freezers. It is not known if the instances are linked. Iran is yet to respond to Barrot’s allegations. Separately on Monday, the Paris prosecutor said an investigation had been opened into the head of an offensive cyber unit associated with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as well as his two deputies. Laure Beccuau named the unit as Shahid Kaveh, which she said had an affiliation with the electronic and cyber centre of the IRGC. On 11 October, hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units used in many of France’s supermarkets. More than 100 of Coopérative U’s supermarkets were hit, as well as 180 stores from Intermarché and its Netto brand. In some stores, temperatures of the fridges reportedly rose to 50C (120F) overnight.

items.title: Nine outstanding players win NASCO prize as Hearts thrash Lions, Chelsea stun Kotoko in GPL Matchweek 10
items.description: Nine outstanding players have been rewarded for their brilliance in Matchweek 10 of the 2026/27 Ghana Premier League, after being named NASCO Man of the Match winners in their respective fixtures. The list, released by the Ghana Football Association, is headlined by FC AshantiGold captain Kojo Twumasi, who stood tall as AshantiGold held Young Apostles FC to a 0-0 draw at the Len Clay Stadium. It was a weekend that had everything – a Hearts of Oak demolition, a stunning Kotoko collapse, late winners, and a tight title race at the top. Hearts Return With A Statement At the University of Ghana Stadium, Hearts of Oak produced their best performance of the season, thrashing Heart of Lions 3-0 . The Phobians wasted no time. Ransford Mensah opened the scoring after just two minutes before John Antwi grabbed a brace to seal a convincing win that lifted Hearts to second place on the table with 20 points. NASCO Man of the Match: Abdul Karim – Hearts of Oak. For Heart of Lions, it was a painful afternoon. The defeat leaves them in 16th place, deep in the relegation fight. Chelsea stun Kotoko in Berekum One of of the stories of weekend came at the Golden City Park, where Berekum Chelsea came from behind to beat Asante Kotoko 2-1. Kotoko looked to be heading for victory when Inusah Adam converted a penalty in the 60th minute to put them ahead. But Chelsea refused to give up. Zacharia Fuseini equalised five minutes later before Yussif Bayanalabe scored a dramatic stoppage-time winner in the 90+1st minute to send the home fans into wild celebrations. NASCO Man of the Match: Emmanuel Ofosu — Berekum Chelsea. The result means Kotoko have now gone three league games without a win, leaving them 10th on the table with 13 points. Medeama stay top, Port City keep pushing Defending champions Medeama SC stayed at the top of the league with a hard-fought 1-0 win over Swedru All Blacks at the TnA Park, thanks to Kingsley Braye’s 38th-minute strike. NASCO Man of the Match: Emmanuel Annor — Medeama SC. Port City FC also continued their dream debut season, beating Basake Holy Stars 1-0 at the Daasebre Boamah Darko II Park. Francis Gyetuah scored the only goal in the 65th minute to keep Port City in third place with 18 points. NASCO Man of the Match: Francis Gyetuah – Port City FC. At the end of Matchweek 10, Medeama SC, Hearts of Oak, Port City FC and FC Samartex occupy the top four positions, while Heart of Lions, Young Apostles and Dreams FC remain in the relegation zone. Drama in Bechem, draws elsewhere At the Nana Fosu Gyeabour Park, Bechem United secured a dramatic 2-1 victory over FC Samartex. Augustine Okrah gave Bechem the lead in the 39th minute, Gabriel Osei equalised for Samartex in the 57th minute, before substitute Dennis Modzaka scored deep into stoppage time in the 90+5th minute to win it for the Hunters. NASCO Man of the Match: Augustine Okrah — Bechem United. Karela were held to a goalless draw by Vision FC in Friday’s only fixture in Tamale. NASCO Man of the Match: Faisal Gariba – Karela United In Obuasi AshantiGold were unable to find a breakthrough against Young Apostles as the two sides settled for a goalless draw. The NASCO Man of the Match was Kojo Twumasi of FC AshantiGold. Bibiani Gold Stars were held at home by Aduana FC at the DUN’s Park in Bibiani. NASCO Man of the Match: Claude Shooting Bortey — Gold Stars. Dreams FC 1-1 Debibi United – Dreams shared the spoils with Debibi United in a 1-1 draw at the Tuba Astro Turf and the NASCO Man of the Match wad Bernard Kokonu of Dreams FC.

items.title: [Décodeur] Je ne crois pas ce que je vois
items.description: Avec l'intelligence artificielle, fabriquer un faux ne prend plus que quelques minutes. Le démenti prend toujours des heures. Face à cette course perdue d'avance, la riposte la plus durable ne se joue pas seulement dans les rédactions : elle se joue dans la tête du public. « Je ne crois que ce que je vois. » La célèbre formule prêtée à l’apôtre saint Thomas a traversé les siècles. Elle a fondé notre rapport à la preuve : une photo, une vidéo, une voix enregistrée valaient témoignage. Tout ce qu’on voit est vrai. Avec l'intelligence artificielle, cette vieille sagesse ne tient plus. Aujourd’hui, voir ne suffit plus, il faut un peu plus : vérifier. On peut désormais voir, entendre… et être trompé. On l'a tous appris à nos dépens. Bienvenue dans l'ère de la désinformation augmentée. Les vieilles recettes de la manipulation existent toujours. Mais elles sont maintenent dopées par une IA générative qui rend ce type de fabrication rapide, bon marché et à la portée de tous. Le 15 février 2025, un audio de plus de quatre minutes envahit X, Facebook, TikTok et les groupes WhatsApp. Présenté comme l'analyse d'un journaliste de RFI et France 24, logos à l'appui, il commente le rapport de la Cour des comptes sur les finances publiques. Le ton est assuré, le format sonne « radio internationale ». Beaucoup y croient. Le problème : RFI n'a jamais diffusé ce contenu. La radio a démenti formellement : la voix ne correspond à aucun de ses journalistes. D’ailleurs Ndeye Fatou Diery Diagne avait fact-checké ce deepfake dans une vidéo publiée sur la page Facebook du Soleil : « Alerte deepfake : l'audio viral attribué à RFI et France 24 est un faux ». La désinformation n'est pas née avec l'IA. Rumeurs, photos sorties de leur contexte, faux communiqués : ils ont toujours existé. Ce qui change, c'est l'échelle. D’où le concept de « désinformation augmentée ». L'IA augmente le faux sur trois plans. D'abord, la vitesse et le volume. Un texte, une image ou une voix de synthèse se fabriquent en quelques minutes, sans compétence technique, souvent gratuitement. Un seul individu peut désormais produire ce qui demandait hier une équipe entière. Ensuite, le réalisme. Le faux ne se contente plus d'affirmer : il montre et il fait entendre. Pendant la présidentielle de 2024, des audios attribués au candidat Amadou Ba ont circulé sur les réseaux avant d'être présentés par la presse comme des montages fabriqués par IA. Et l'audio RFI n'est pas un cas isolé : Reporters sans frontières a recensé d'autres faux attribués à RFI et France 24, au Cameroun et en RDC. On ne pirate plus seulement des visages : on pirate la confiance accordée aux médias. Enfin, la proximité. L'IA parle désormais nos langues. Un faux en wolof, diffusé par note vocale dans un groupe de famille, passe sous les radars des plateformes et des vérificateurs, qui travaillent d'abord en français ou en anglais. Il y a un effet plus pervers encore. Quand tout peut être truqué, plus rien n'est cru. Un responsable pris en flagrant délit peut crier au « deepfake » pour se dédouaner. C’est ce que les chercheurs appellent le « dividende du menteur ». Le doute généralisé profite à ceux qui ont quelque chose à cacher, dit-on. Face à cela, le fact-checking reste indispensable. C'est une belle contribution dans la lutte contre la désinformation. Mais il a une limite structurelle : il arrive après. Fabriquer un faux prend quelques minutes. Le vérifier, le documenter et publier un démenti prend des heures. C’est un genre lent. Pendant ce temps, le mensonge a déjà fait son chemin, et le démenti ne touchera jamais tous ceux qui ont vu le faux. Aucun acteur ne peut gagner seul. Les plateformes doivent étiqueter les contenus générés par IA et être transparentes. Les autorités doivent réguler et porter des politiques d'éducation. Les rédactions doivent renforcer leurs protocoles de vérification. Mais un seul levier agit directement sur le public : l'éducation aux médias et à l'information, l'EMI. L'EMI ne dit pas aux gens quoi penser. Elle leur donne des outils pour s'informer, évaluer et partager de façon responsable. C'est le principe du « prebunking » : apprendre à reconnaître les techniques de manipulation avant d'y être exposé, comme un vaccin plutôt qu'un remède. Au Sénégal, le chantier reste largement ouvert. Les médias ont un rôle à jouer. Au Soleil Digital, nous essayons d'y contribuer avec Soleil Check pour la vérification et 100 % IA pour la vulgarisation. Mais il faut aller plus loin : former les enseignants et les journalistes, intégrer l'EMI à l'école, et parler aux communautés dans leurs langues, par les relais en qui elles ont confiance : radios communautaires, associations, lieux de culte. Ps : cette chronique a été corrigée par l’IA. Abdou Khadir SECK

items.title: Man Utd delay decision on Carrick’s future after dropping into relegation zone — report
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United are not in a hurry to sack head coach Michael Carrick despite their drop into the Premier League relegation zone following Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, according to Sky Sports . Sky Sports News reports that the club’s hierarchy plan to use the international break to assess the team’s poor start to the season and reconsider their options before making a decision on Carrick’s future. The former United midfielder is under increasing pressure after the club recorded just one win in 11 matches, conceded 30 goals in all competitions and endured what has been described as their worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign. United’s 4-4 draw against Villa followed another comeback in their previous match, but the recent results have not been enough to ease concerns over their overall performances. Carrick and his players were given Monday off after the Villa encounter, with the head coach and his staff expected to return to the club’s Carrington training base on Tuesday. With several players away on international duty and no first-team training sessions scheduled in the coming days, the break is expected to give the club’s leadership time to conduct a broader review. According to Sky Sports, three major factors have contributed to the hierarchy’s decision not to rush a change in the dugout. First, United supporters have not called for Carrick to be dismissed, with the former midfielder still enjoying considerable affection from the fanbase because of his achievements as a player. Carrick won 11 major trophies during his playing career at Old Trafford, including the Champions League and five Premier League titles. Secondly, the club’s hierarchy believe the 45-year-old still has the support of the dressing room, despite the team’s poor form. The recent comebacks against Roma in the Champions League and Aston Villa in the Premier League are understood to have reinforced the belief that the players have not given up on their manager. Thirdly, United’s decision-makers are reportedly not convinced that replacing Carrick would automatically resolve the team’s problems, with the performances of the players also under scrutiny. The report adds that the club could consider available managerial options, including Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe, if they eventually decide to make a change. For now, however, United are expected to take their time before deciding whether Carrick remains the right man to lead the club out of their current crisis. items.title: Joe Biden scales back book tour as cancer ‘slows me down’
items.description: Former US president Joe Biden says he is scaling back plans to promote his upcoming memoir as he battles aggressive prostate cancer, acknowledging that the illness sometimes leaves him struggling. The 83-year-old Democrat, whose health was a major issue during his presidency, said Sunday that he would be unable to make as many public appearances as he had hoped ahead of the November 17 release of “Promise Me, America.” “Some days are better than others. It hasn’t stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down,” Biden wrote on X. “What that means is, unfortunately, I won’t be able to do as many conversations about my book as I’d hoped. However, I’m hopeful the words on the page speak for themselves.” Biden announced in May 2025, four months after leaving the White House, that he had been diagnosed with an aggressive form of prostate cancer that had spread to his bones. He has since undergone radiation and hormone therapy, while his son Hunter said in August that the disease had spread further and was causing considerable pain. Biden struck an optimistic note about his treatment, saying his doctors “continue to be encouraged” by his response. His memoir chronicles his four years in the White House, including his handling of the Covid-19 pandemic, wars in Afghanistan and Ukraine, and his controversial decision to seek reelection in 2024 before withdrawing. In an excerpt published Monday by The Atlantic, Biden delivered a blistering attack on his successor Donald Trump over the 2021 assault on the US Capitol by supporters seeking to overturn Trump’s election defeat. “What Trump did on January 6, 2021, should never be forgotten. It should follow him to his grave,” Biden wrote. He also recalled an unexpectedly friendly Oval Office meeting with Trump following the Republican’s 2024 election victory, during which his successor suggested they might have been friends outside politics. Biden abandoned his reelection campaign in July 2024 after a disastrous debate against Trump intensified concerns about his age and fitness for office. His vice president, Kamala Harris, subsequently lost the election, returning Trump to the White House. Biden said his book would explain the decisions he made in office and reflect his faith in American democracy. items.title: Waltersmith, FIRST E&P, Sahara Group & SNEPCO Partner Women in Energy Network for 2026 Gala
items.description: Women in Energy Network marks six years of advancing women’s participation and leadership with the launch of a landmark DEI Benchmark developed in partnership with KPMG. On Wednesday, 11 November 2026, the Women in Energy Network (WIEN) will convene some of the most influential executives, policymakers, and institutions in Nigeria’s energy landscape for its inaugural WIEN Gala & Awards 2026 , held at The Metropolitan Club, Victoria Island, Lagos. Corporate and individual reservations are now open at https://bit.ly/wiengala . The milestone evening celebrates six years of WIEN’s institutional impact in strengthening female participation, executive visibility, and enterprise growth across the energy value chain. The gala is hosted by Dr Cecilia Umoren, Chair of the WIEN Board of Trustees and Executive Chairman of Millennium Oil and Gas Company Limited, and convened by Engr. Tony Attah, Managing Director/CEO of Renaissance Africa Energy Company Limited. Established in 2020, WIEN has transitioned qualitative advocacy into structured sector development, equipping women professionals and business owners through mentorship pipelines, capacity-building frameworks, and cross-sector stakeholder collaboration. “For us at WIEN, advancing women’s participation in the energy sector must go beyond advocacy; it must be supported by evidence, measurable outcomes, and sustained institutional commitment. The numbers make the case clearly,” said Dr Cecilia Umoren , Chair of the WIEN Board of Trustees. “Globally, data from the International Energy Agency (IEA) shows women account for roughly 20% of the energy workforce and barely 12% of senior executive leadership roles. Closer to home, domestic audit data from NEITI reveal that women make up only about 18% of Nigeria’s extractive sector workforce, with technical disciplines and STEM pipelines trailing even further behind. These figures highlight the urgent need to strengthen pathways from technical education into employment, entrepreneurship, and executive governance.” Underlining the strategic pivot toward empirical tracking, Mrs Eyono Fatayi-Williams, President of WIEN , added: “This is why the WIEN DEI Benchmark, developed in partnership with KPMG , is so important. We want organisations to have a clearer basis for understanding their current position, identifying gaps and tracking progress. Inclusion must become something we can assess, measure and improve. Our goal is to see more women-owned businesses participating in the energy value chain, more women progressing into senior leadership, and more organisations translating their commitments into tangible opportunities. This is the next phase of WIEN’s work, and we invite the entire industry to be part of it.” An Evening of Recognition, Influence and Industry Dialogue Beyond the benchmark launch, the 2026 WIEN Gala & Awards will celebrate the individuals and organisations making a meaningful difference across Nigeria’s energy sector. The evening will feature a keynote address by Dr Mutiu Sunmonu , alongside reflections on WIEN’s six-year journey, including a milestone presentation and highlights of the Network’s work and impact. Guests will also have opportunities to connect through a red-carpet reception, networking, media interviews, and goodwill messages from distinguished industry stakeholders. More than a celebration, the Gala brings together the people and institutions shaping the industry’s future, creating room for conversations, relationships, and collaborations that can extend well beyond the evening. Industry Partnerships Driving Lasting Impact The growing support for the 2026 WIEN Gala reflects the importance of collective industry action in advancing a more inclusive energy ecosystem. Leading the coalition of partners are Renaissance Africa Energy Company JV, NLNG Limited, SNEPCO, and Telmek Global Resources , alongside Waltersmith Petroman Oil Limited, FIRST E&P, and Sahara Group as Platinum Sponsors. Gold Sponsors include ND Western Limited, Virgin Forest Energy, Bank of Industry, Aradel Holdings Plc, and NEXIM Bank , while Tetracore Energy Group, Loyz Marine , and Eko Electricity Distribution Plc (EKEDC) join as Silver Sponsors. Together, these organisations represent a cross-section of the energy and financial ecosystem, demonstrating the value of collaboration and sustained attention still needed to advance an industry-wide conversation on leadership, executive representation and participation in strategic decision-making. “We are deeply grateful to the organisations, brands and individuals who have partnered with us to make the 2026 WIEN Gala & Awards possible,” says Bassey Adie , Director of Partnerships & Conferences and Chairperson of the Gala Planning Committee. “Their support goes beyond backing a flagship event; it reflects a shared belief in the importance of building a more inclusive, competitive, and sustainable energy sector. Partnerships like these create platforms for meaningful engagement, open doors to new opportunities, and strengthen the collective effort to ensure more women can participate, lead, and thrive across the energy value chain.” “As we celebrate six years of WIEN, we look forward to building on these relationships and welcoming more organisations and industry leaders who share our vision for the future”, said Fatayi-Williams , reaffirming the network’s forward momentum. “The WIEN Gala & Awards 2026 promises to be a defining moment in our Network’s journey, celebrating how far the industry has come while setting a more ambitious course for what comes next”. Individual professionals, corporate executives, and sector organisations intending to attend can book tickets or corporate tables directly at https://bit.ly/wiengala — ENDS — Media Contacts & Event Enquiries: Secretariat, Women in Energy Network | info@wien.com.ng The post Waltersmith, FIRST E&P, Sahara Group & SNEPCO Partner Women in Energy Network for 2026 Gala appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ghana in final talks with Boeing over revival of national airline – Victor Smith
items.description: Ghana’s Ambassador to the United States, Victor Smith, says negotiations with Boeing over the establishment of a national airline are nearing completion. Speaking in an interview on JoyNews, Mr Smith said the government was working to finalise arrangements to revive the national carrier, with efforts also underway to attract investors to the project. “We are looking for investors. They may invest in this effort. They may get something out of it. What is important for me is the legacy that the President will leave when he’s leaving office—that we will have a national flag back in the air. That is important for me,” he said. Mr Smith said there was considerable public interest in the return of a national airline, arguing that many Ghanaians would welcome the opportunity to travel with a carrier bearing the country’s flag. “Ghanaians are more excited flying their own flag than flying British Airways or Delta or United and being charged huge amounts for tickets. They think that we would feel more comfortable and fly in our own flag,” he said. The Ambassador said discussions with Boeing had reached an advanced stage, although he did not provide details of the proposed agreement or indicate when it would be concluded. “We are in talks with Boeing. The deal is nearing completion. We are working to ensure that Ghana has a national airline that we can all be proud of,” he stated. Ghana has been without a national airline since the collapse of Ghana Airways in 2004 and Ghana International Airlines in 2010. Successive governments have explored options for establishing a new national carrier, including partnerships with international aviation companies. The latest effort is aimed at restoring a national airline, although details of its ownership structure, financing, operational model and expected launch date have yet to be provided.

items.title: Ghana’s film industry woes go beyond marketing – Selassie Ibrahim
items.description: Founder of the REFFA Awards, Selassie Ibrahim, has urged Ghanaians to change their attitude towards locally produced films. She has therefore blamed negative perceptions and poor patronage for the challenges facing the country’s movie industry. Speaking to Kwame Dadzie on Joy FM’s Showbiz A-Z , she said the problem goes beyond marketing. She rather argued that many Ghanaians dismiss local productions without even watching them. She compared Ghana’s attitude towards local films with the support Nigerian audiences give their own productions, stressing that reviving the industry requires collective efforts from filmmakers and the public. “It is not about failing to deploy the right tools to reach the Ghanaian consumer. My observation is that anything made in Ghana is often considered not good enough. People do not even take the time to watch and appreciate whether there has been improvement. They simply conclude that it is not good”, she said. Drawing a comparison with Nigeria, where she said audiences readily support local productions, Selassie noted that Nigerians demonstrate a stronger commitment to their own content. “I live in Nigeria and work there frequently. You will hardly find them turning away from their own content, even on DStv. They love their own and patronise it. No matter what, they want to support their own. But in Ghana, the opposite is often the case,” the filmmaker noted. She urged Ghanaians to make a conscious effort to patronise local films, particularly those showing in cinemas, explaining that audience support is essential to sustaining film production. “We are only pleading with Ghanaians to start watching our content. Go to the cinemas, watch our movies and encourage us to produce more. If I invest in a film and cannot recover even my initial investment, how do I go back on set to produce another one?” Selassie explained that poor returns on film investments make it difficult for producers to raise funds for subsequent projects and deliver the quality of productions audiences expect. “You cannot give people the kind of content they want when you have not been able to sell your previous production or even recover your capital. You end up producing with whatever resources you have available, just to keep going.” She, however, insisted that Ghanaian filmmakers have the talent and storytelling ability to produce quality films if they receive the necessary financial and audience support. “It is not that we cannot produce good content. Ghana has authentic stories to tell. We are intentional and detailed in our storytelling. But when you are not producing regularly, you become rusty. It is like acting, scriptwriting or driving; when you stop practising, you lose that sharpness.” While appealing to the public for greater support, Selassie acknowledged that filmmakers must also improve their business practices and take responsibility for the industry’s growth. “We also have a role to play. We must learn to put our books together and do things properly. It has to be a collective effort between filmmakers, investors and the Ghanaian public.”

items.title: Musique : L’artiste Naeti dédicace son premier album « Lahana »
items.description: L'artiste musicien Abraham Tindano, connu sous le nom de Naeti, alias Sapino la Merveille, a procédé samedi 7 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou à la dédicace de son premier album intitulé « Lahana » qui signifie « bien » en langue gulmancema. Composé de neuf morceaux, l'opus mêle différentes sonorités et compositions, dont certaines portent une histoire particulièrement personnelle pour l'artiste. « Lahana », « Wawaala », « Nanga », « Prince Timothée », « Buama », « Saala », « Danser », « Your » et « Nissaalo » constituent la tracklist du premier album de Naeti, alias Sapino la Merveille, « Lahana ». À travers celui-ci, le message de Naeti se veut clair : « faire le bien n'est jamais inutile ». Parmi ces neuf titres, « Your » occupe une place singulière dans le parcours artistique et personnel de l'artiste. L'artiste Naeti (au milieu) dédicace son premier album « Lahana » Composé et enregistré en 2013 au studio Bonne Nouvelle de Prince Édouard Ouédraogo, ce morceau était à l'origine une chanson d'amour dédiée à celle qui partageait alors la vie de l'artiste. Sa compagne, avec laquelle il a vécu pendant six années, était la destinataire de cette déclaration musicale exprimant son affection et la place particulière qu'elle occupait dans son cœur. Selon Abraham Tindano, le temps a profondément changé la portée de « Your ». La disparition de sa bien-aimée a laissé une absence douloureuse et des souvenirs auxquels l'artiste reste attachée. Initialement écrite comme une déclaration d'amour, la chanson est devenue au fil des années un témoignage musical de leur histoire. Avec « Lahana », Naeti ne propose donc pas seulement un ensemble de neuf chansons. À travers « Your », l'artiste partage une partie de son histoire personnelle, rappelant que certaines mélodies dépassent le simple cadre du divertissement pour devenir les témoins d'une vie et de sentiments qui traversent le temps. Le public à ma dédicace L'album est vendu à 5 000 FCFA et disponible auprès de l'artiste ou de son équipe. « J'invite mes fans et les mélomanes à se le procurer et à me soutenir jusqu'au bout. Ce sont leurs encouragements qui m'ont accompagné jusque-là. Je profite également de l'occasion pour les remercier pour leur confiance », a lancé l'artiste Naeti. items.title: Achraf Hakimi dans le onze mondial FIFPRO 2026
items.description: Achraf Hakimi continue de s’installer parmi les références mondiales à son poste. Le capitaine des Lions de l’Atlas et latéral droit du Paris Saint-Germain a été retenu dans le onze mondial de l’année 2026 de la FIFPRO, dévoilé ce lundi 9 novembre. Une nouvelle reconnaissance pour le défenseur marocain, qui figure pour la deuxième année consécutive dans l’équipe type mondiale de la FIFPRO. Hakimi confirme ainsi sa place parmi les meilleurs latéraux droits de la planète, au terme d’une année particulièrement riche sur le plan collectif et individuel. Le joueur du PSG apparaît aux côtés de plusieurs grandes stars du football mondial, notamment Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal et Jude Bellingham. Il partage également cette sélection avec son coéquipier parisien Nuno Mendes. Cette distinction vient récompenser une saison 2026 marquée par plusieurs succès majeurs pour le capitaine marocain. Avec le Paris Saint-Germain, Achraf Hakimi a notamment remporté la Ligue des champions ainsi que le championnat de France, contribuant pleinement aux performances du club parisien. Sous le maillot des Lions de l’Atlas, le latéral droit a également été l’un des cadres de la sélection marocaine lors de la Coupe du monde 2026, où le Maroc a atteint les quarts de finale. The 2026 FIFPRO Men’s #World11 Decided exclusively by 19,806 professional men’s footballers worldwide. By the players, for the players pic.twitter.com/MnHEMHxtf1 — FIFPRO (@FIFPRO) November 9, 2026 Déjà présent dans le onze mondial de la FIFPRO en 2025, Achraf Hakimi renouvelle donc sa présence parmi les joueurs les plus plébiscités par ses pairs. Cette sélection vient confirmer la régularité du défenseur, devenu au fil des saisons une référence à son poste grâce à son activité offensive, sa vitesse, sa capacité à répéter les efforts et son influence dans les grands rendez-vous. items.title: ‘Our young people are afraid of their shadows abroad’ – Ambassador Smith
items.description: Ghana’s Ambassador to the United States, Victor Smith, says some young Ghanaians living abroad are struggling with difficult conditions, including unemployment and fear, and has urged them to consider returning home with investors to create opportunities. He cited the Ghanaian community in Worcester, Massachusetts, where he estimates about 45,000 Ghanaians live, as an example of the challenges facing members of the diaspora. Speaking in a one-on-one interview with Desmond Danso on JoyNews, Ambassador Smith said some Ghanaians in the city were not working and appeared to live in fear. “I went to Worcester in Massachusetts and there are about 45,000 Ghanaians in Worcester alone. And ask me whether they are working. No. They’re not. And they are even afraid of their shadows that ICE will pick them. So, they are spending most of their time in their churches,” he said. The Ambassador encouraged Ghanaians abroad who are considering returning home to explore partnerships with investors to establish businesses and create jobs. He said such arrangements could provide opportunities for young people and help reduce the pressure to migrate in search of better prospects. “These are not easy things. And I am preaching to them that listen, I’m here to do this. When opportunity strikes, go back home by all means. Go with an investor and try to pick up the pieces. It is possible,” he said. Ambassador Smith said creating more employment opportunities in Ghana would help reduce migration among young people. “We create jobs and opportunities for the young people so that our young people, at least, the migration will be minimised,” he said. He has been engaging members of the Ghanaian diaspora and investors in the United States to promote investment opportunities in sectors including mining, energy, agriculture and manufacturing. The government has also been encouraging Ghanaians abroad to invest in the country’s development.

items.title: Ghana’s traditional economic model has failed to deliver – Ato Forson
items.description: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has described Ghana’s traditional economic model as unsuccessful in delivering the desired development outcomes for citizens over the past 69 years, calling for a fundamental shift towards sustainable economic growth and job creation. He said the government’s proposed New Economy initiative was designed to transform the country’s economic structure, create sustainable employment and provide better opportunities for the growing number of young people entering the labour market. Dr Forson made the remarks when he addressed the National House of Chiefs ahead of the presentation of the 2027 Budget to Parliament on Thursday, November 12, 2026. He urged traditional leaders to support the government’s economic agenda, arguing that Ghana could no longer depend on approaches that had failed to generate sufficient jobs and improve living standards. The Finance Minister said temporary employment interventions such as the National Builders Corps (NABCO) and the Youth Employment Agency (YEA) could provide immediate relief but were not sustainable solutions to the country’s unemployment challenge. “The temporary models may offer immediate relief and experience to our people, but our young people need dependable livelihoods beyond the end of the placement of these temporary models. Their future cannot depend on moving from one temporary opportunity to the next,” he said. Dr Forson said the government was instead seeking to build an economy capable of generating lasting employment and expanding opportunities for young Ghanaians. He also called for a shift from the export of raw materials towards domestic processing and value addition, saying the approach would help create jobs, strengthen local industries and increase the economic benefits derived from Ghana’s natural resources. He further assured the chiefs that the government would maintain fiscal discipline and ensure prudent management of public funds. He said value for money would remain a key consideration in government spending as part of efforts to support the country’s economic transformation. Dr Forson appealed to the National House of Chiefs and other stakeholders to support the New Economy initiative as the government prepares to present its 2027 Budget.
